title: Settings boot lands on a blank 'provider server tools' view instead of the providers list — first-click UX broken
description:
Owner bug report 2026-09-04 (urgent — about to distribute to first users): clicking the Settings button for the first time lands on a view that just says 'provider server tools' instead of showing the list of providers. The user can't configure their provider because they're stuck on the wrong view.

ROOT CAUSE (likely): the multi-section navigation change (0181699e) introduced lazy section rendering. The first Settings click may land on a section hash that maps to the server-tools sub-panel rather than the main providers list. Combined with the wuvg fix (initProviderServerTools called from ensureSectionRendered('providers')), the server-tools sub-panel may be rendering as the only visible content when the full providers section (with the provider list, API key entry, model picker) should be showing.

FIX: the first Settings click should ALWAYS land on the main providers list (the provider entries with API key fields and model pickers), NOT a sub-panel. The default section hash should be #providers pointing to the full provider management view.

ACCEPTANCE (falsification-gated): fresh install → click Settings → see the providers list (not server tools); enter an API key; press Use; the model is configured. A first user can go from zero to a working agent in under 60 seconds.
notes: 2026-09-05 pi lane: the blank-boot P0 was already fixed on main by 7ff2f479 (09-05 05:59). Verified empirically: parent d898d687 boots to provider-panels with 0 children (the reported blank 'provider server tools' view); HEAD renders tabs+panels+API-key fields through plain tab, #providers hash, and the embedded hub Settings view. Root cause: empty hash normalized to falsy so boot never called ensureSectionRendered('providers') while the panel was statically active. Harness blind spot closed on branch cap-beads-hy91 @ 3748b196 (content assertion, falsification-proven).
close_reason: Verified fixed on main by 7ff2f479 (hash-default root cause shared with hdbi); harness blind spot closed with content assertions @ b44c2cde (falsification: revert leaves visibility green, content check RED {tabs:0,panels:0,keyFields:0}). k3 empirical before/after.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED in a real loaded extension (not the multi-section change, not the wuvg server-tools fix).

The hub's Settings button opens options/options.html with NO fragment (extension/ntp/ntp.js:3666); Chrome's own extension Options entry does the same. navigationController.syncCurrent() routed that through handleHashChange, which fails closed when normalizeSettingsSectionId() returns null — correct for a mid-session navigation, fatal on boot: ensureSectionRendered() never ran for ANY section. options.html marks #providers class='panel active' statically, so the panel was visible but completely unbuilt. With developer features on, the only thing still painting inside it is the static 'Provider server tools' card — which is why the owner read it as a provider-server-tools view.

Measured (fresh profile, headless):
  options.html            -> tabs 0, panels 0, provider cards 0
  options.html#providers  -> tabs 1, panels 4, provider cards 7

FIX (branch cap-hy91-settings-boot, off origin/main@d6019129):
- extension/lib/navigation-controller.js: opt-in defaultHash; syncCurrent() falls back to it when the current hash is absent or unresolvable. Mid-session navigate() to an unknown hash still fails closed.
- extension/options/options.js: defaultHash: '#providers'.
- extension/options/options.js: ensureSectionRendered() took its one-shot claim BEFORE awaiting the renderer, so a renderer that threw left that section blank for the life of the page with no retry. The claim is released on failure and the error rethrown.

GATES:
- tests/navigation-controller.test.ts 15/15 (4 new boot tests). Falsification: reverted the syncCurrent fallback -> the two boot tests RED -> restored -> GREEN 15/15.
- tests/settings-section-navigation.test.ts 7/7 (2 new source gates).
- scripts/kat-settings-multi-section.ts: its 'initial load' check asserted only PANEL VISIBILITY, which is exactly why it stayed green through this bug. It now asserts rendered provider cards + key fields + tab strip, and adds a stale-deep-link fallback check. 3/3 RED on the pre-fix bundle; re-running on the rebuilt one.
- build clean; check:vocabulary / check:gallery / check:reachability / check:changelog / check:changelog-order all OK.

title: Remove ALL self-imposed size caps across tools, storage, transport, and rendering (owner directive: unlimited)
description:
OWNER DIRECTIVE 2026-09-03 (Telegram, emphatic): 'Don't discard anything, don't limit... Unlimited. I hate all these weird constraints for output and tools and tool call message... there's no real rational argument for why the limits have been chosen. There's been no evidence gathered about what limits should be... This is my extension doing the things I need it to do... No limits please.'

SCOPE: every SELF-IMPOSED size bound in our code. Known inventory (audit to complete this list):
- Tool-argument contract caps (extension/lib/tool-argument-contract.js — per-call byte caps on tool args)
- fs read transport caps (MAX_FS_READ_BYTES 10MiB window cap; MAX_FS_TEXT_DECODE_BYTES 2MiB diff-card decode)
- artifact bounds: 64KiB per-call append cap, 256KiB/4MiB artifact ceilings, serialized-value bound routing
- sandbox preview host 300,000-char discard (p45y finding; removal steered into the p45y r5 revise)
- memory-store per-value/per-store bounds (MAX_VALUE_BYTES 256KiB family; MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES/MAX_THREAD_BYTES threads caps; memory.js:221 8MiB store cap — kmpq started this: payloads by reference; finish removing the rest)
- journalEntry.id 200-char bound, name/description length caps in workflows save
- any MAX_* / maxBytes / char-slice bounds in extension/lib + extension/shared

RULES:
1. REMOVE self-imposed caps outright. Where a REAL platform constraint exists (browser message size, OPFS quota, storage quota), do NOT fake a smaller cap: route around it (chunking, by-reference payloads — the kmpq pattern) and surface the PLATFORM's honest error when the platform itself refuses.
2. The default becomes: store/return/attach COMPLETE data. No 'bounded limit' language anywhere in tool errors.
3. Each removal ships with a falsification test proving the formerly-capped operation succeeds at sizes past the old bound (use the owner's real repro shapes: 9KB reads, 10MiB responses, append-grown artifacts).
4. Keep SECURITY bounds that are not size-related (path traversal, origin-keying, approval gates) — this directive is about SIZE limits only.
5. Audit deliverable: a bead comment listing every constant found, its classification (removed / platform-routed / security-non-size), and the test proving it.

Related already-landed steps: jb0a (read_file), kmpq (journal complete-storage), p45y in-flight (append + preview cap removal). This bead is the umbrella for finishing the sweep everywhere else.

Legend: **SELF-IMPOSED** → remove (nothing platform requires it) · **PLATFORM-REAL** → keep bound, route around (chunk/by-reference) + surface the platform's honest error · **SECURITY-NON-SIZE** → keep (not a size limit). Bounded-history/ring designs are flagged **OWNER-STEER** (removal = unbounded memory growth; the directive says unlimited, so listed as SELF-IMPOSED with the risk called out).

## Summary

- **SELF-IMPOSED → remove: ~60 bounds** (T1-T24, T27-T29 partial, S1-S6, S9, S11-S13?, S15-S20, R1-R9, R11, R12, D1, D6; plus the six verified prior-claim items)
- **PLATFORM-REAL → keep bound + route/honest error: 4** (T25 segment length, T26 getRandomValues 65536, R10 OPFS segment, plus chrome.runtime practical message limits as they surface)
- **SECURITY-NON-SIZE → keep: ~15** (capability counts, approval/pending queues, permission structures, untrusted-fence depth, fetch-policy host list, path traversal guards, id/charset grammars, delegation budgets — none are size limits)
- **OWNER-STEER subset inside SELF-IMPOSED: ~10** (bounded-history rings/retention: journal count, board log, usage ledger, cap-log ring, diagnostics ring, version counts, CAS retention, quarantine lists — removing these changes product memory behavior; recommend archive-to-file instead of drop)
- **OWNED BY np64 (r5), inventory only: 3** (S13 artifact append cap, D2 preview 300k discard, D3 preview count)
- **NOT SIZE (flow/runaway/identity guards), keep: ~12** (host-call counts, dispatch-per-event, retry counts, hash prefixes, lease times, iteration budgets)
- **Stale bead reference: 1** (workflows name/description caps — already gone from the tree)

title: [P0] Saving an API key fails in embedded Settings: credential route treats the embedded surface as non-Settings; inline script CSP-blocked; error string passed as the API key
description:
Owner-reported P0, 2026-09-02 (repro + console evidence):

Repro: open the hub (NTP), open Settings via the embedded view (options.html?embedded=1), Providers section, paste a Gemini API key, save. Result: 'Failed — provider credential routes are restricted to the Settings surface — Check the API key in Settings → Providers — it is missing, invalid, or revoked.' EVEN THOUGH the user IS in Settings → Providers.

Console evidence:
1. CSP violations: "Executing inline script violates the following Content Security Policy directive 'script-src 'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'" for options.html?embedded=1:9 — an inline script in the embedded Settings page is BLOCKED. The embedded boot path likely never runs, so the page cannot prove it is the Settings surface.
2. The smoking gun: the subsequent fetch is generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models?key=Failed%20%E2%80%94%20provider%20credential%20routes... — the ERROR STRING was passed as the API key. The page-side code caught the route refusal and used the refusal text as the credential value.

ROOT CAUSE (hypothesis to verify): the credential-route surface check (provider credential routes 'restricted to the Settings surface') inspects the requesting document/surface — the embedded Settings iframe (options.html?embedded=1) fails that check, probably because its boot script (inline, CSP-blocked) never stamped the surface attestation, or because the embedded=1 boot path is classified as non-Settings. Fix BOTH layers:
(a) Remove the inline script from options.html (move to the external boot bundle) so CSP never blocks it;
(b) Fix the surface classifier so options.html?embedded=1 — the REAL Settings surface — passes the credential-route check (the check should accept the settings document by URL/origin regardless of embedding, or consume the boot-stamped attestation).

ACCEPTANCE (falsification-gated): adding a Gemini (and OpenAI-class) key from the EMBEDDED Settings surface succeeds end-to-end (key stored, models list fetch uses the real key); the CSP console violation is gone; the surface check still REFUSES credential routes from genuinely non-Settings surfaces (that regression test must exist and stay green); no inline scripts in any html page (vocabulary/CSP lint). Tests: provider surface-check route tests with an embedded=1 document double; CSP lint over html files.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text: ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED (upgraded analysis; the inline-CSP theory was secondary): this is a regression from the one-shell merge (2cc00604) — openView now appends ?embedded=1 to every embedded view frame URL (options.html?embedded=1). The owner-surface authorization isExactOptionsSender (extension/lib/pure.js:830) accepts ONLY the bare options.html URL or options.html#<closed-set fragment> — a QUERY STRING never matches (the second branch requires the URL suffix to be exactly a #fragment from OPTIONS_PRODUCT_HASHES). So the embedded Settings page's principal never becomes owner-options and EVERY owner route fails: provider credentials (routes/auth.js:12), tool-catalog diagnostics (SW:5013 — the second symptom the owner reported), tool preview (SW:5033), factory reset (SW:5999,6022). The inline-script CSP violation in the owner's console is a real but SEPARATE pre-existing issue; the auth break is the query-param equality. FIX DIRECTION: normalize the embedded document's URL at boot (history.replaceState to pathname + hash, dropping ?embedded=1) so the sender URL returns to the exact authorized form, OR extend the closed-set check to accept exactly '?embedded=1' (and '?embedded=1#<fragment>') as a product-owned query — the boot-normalize approach is preferred because it keeps sender-URL equality strict regardless of future params. Same acceptance: embedded Settings saves keys, lists tools, previews tools; non-Settings surfaces still refused (regression test).

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text: MERGED to origin/main @ 2afd3910 (lane cap-csp-inline-fix, commits a19f9796 + 7ba15959 + ce7b32c8). Root cause fixed at the boot layer: embedded-boot.js (shared, external — CSP-safe) sets data-embedded then strips ?embedded=1 via history.replaceState inside iframes, so the document URL returns to the exact form isExactOptionsSender authorizes. Embedded Settings regains owner-options: saving API keys, tool-catalog diagnostics, tool preview all work from the hub again. Non-Settings surfaces are still refused (the exact-document + closed-set-fragment checks are unchanged). Gates on the merged tree: build PASS, full suite 3119/0. Also landed: the CSP lint (no shipped page may carry an inline script — data-src smuggle case covered) and the shared boot file.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text: Owner-confirmed: fails on a FRESH Settings panel too (not panel reuse). Narrows to the live request path: identity binding, the provider.test route itself, or the network call it makes. Browser-driven instrumented repro in flight.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text: ROOT CAUSE (final, confirmed by browser-driven repro + landed fix): Chrome reports an iframe's COMMITTED url (query included) as sender.url on runtime messages — so the earlier boot-time history.replaceState strip could never change what the service worker saw, and isExactOptionsSender kept rejecting the embedded Settings document. THE FIX (cap-p0-provider @ 98134e38, merged to origin/main @ d4265234): embedded views now boot at their EXACT canonical URL with no query at all (openView no longer appends ?embedded=1; embeddedness self-detects via window.self !== top; legacy stored routes with the marker are normalized), and the route error classifier names surface refusals honestly (SettingsSurfaceRequiredError → surface/permission recovery copy) — a surface refusal NEVER reads as provider key blame again. Gates on the merged tree: build PASS, full suite green. Owner instructions: pull, npm run build, reload the unpacked extension, reopen Settings from the hub, Test connection. If the test still fails it will now say the REAL reason (e.g. network/host permission) instead of key blame.

title: [CAP-FB-20260901-READ-PAGE-HOST-GRANT-01] read_page on a site without host access returns a raw Chrome error instead of the Allow card
description:
## [CAP-FB-20260901-READ-PAGE-HOST-GRANT-01] read_page on a site without host access returns a raw Chrome error instead of the Allow card
- Feedback: 2026-09-01 — owner's run log: `execute_tool:2` → `read_page` on tab 1840671856 returned `{"error":"Cannot access contents of the page. Extension manifest must request permission to access the respective host."}`; no permission card appeared, the model moved on, and the digest silently omitted that site. "I can't see the error in the UI".
- Updated: 2026-09-01 22:23 UTC
- Status: OPEN
- Resume: —
- Priority: P0
- Owner: model worker (Fable 5 subagent) under the reanalysis coordinator session — CLAIMED; do not start a parallel attempt
- Workspace: active (local path private)
- Branch: `cap/read-page-host-grant` (pushed to origin as the candidate branch; merged by the coordinator)
- Base: `ffaac6af`
- Candidate: —
- Shipping: —
- Acceptance: `read_page` (and every tool that injects into a page: the page-action family, `capture_screenshot`) on an origin the extension has no host access for returns the structured permission denial (`permissionDenial(..., {grantOrigins:[origin]})`) so ONE Allow card renders in the conversation naming the site; Allow grants that origin via `chrome.permissions.request` on the owner's click and the run resumes and reads the page; Deny leaves a readable error line ("Not allowed to read example.com — you declined") on the card. Privileged URLs (`chrome://`, the Web Store) still fail closed with the existing message. The raw Chrome string never reaches the model or the owner.
  - Context: `CAP-FB-20260830-HOST-ACCESS-STORY-01` (DONE) made host access optional, so a fresh profile has NO host permissions. `extension/lib/browser-tools.js:923` `readPage` checks only `hasScriptingPermission()` (`:925`) then calls `chrome.scripting.executeScript` (`:932`); the host-permission failure is caught at `:946` and returned as `{error: String(e.message)}` — a plain error, not the `permissionDenial` shape that `CAP-FB-20260830-DENIAL-TO-GRANT-CARD-01` (DONE) turns into the in-conversation Allow card (compare `close_tab` at `browser-tools.js:2248-2252`, which returns `permissionDenial(..., {grantOrigins:[origin]})`). `agent.js:1052` `onPermissionRequest` blocks the run on that shape until the owner decides, and the SW persists `permissionRequirement` on the row (`service-worker.js:2678-2688`) so a reopened thread re-renders the card. What must NOT change: the privileged-URL block (PRIVILEGED-URL-BLOCK-01); the browser-control grant semantics (host access ≠ browser control — reading a page needs host access + `scripting`; acting needs browser control too); one card per distinct origin per run (the card dedupes on `requirement.key`).
  - Reproduce today: fresh profile, real provider, open `https://example.com`, run "Read the page in the example.com tab and summarise it" → the tool card (if visible) says "Cannot access contents of the page…", no Allow card, the model apologises.
  - Files: `extension/lib/browser-tools.js` (`readPage` 923: resolve the target tab, derive `canonicalOrigin(tab.url)`, `chrome.permissions.contains({origins:[origin + "/*"]})` → if false return `permissionDenial("host access not granted for <origin>", {reason: "read the page on <host>", grantOrigins:[origin], permissions:["scripting"]})`; the same pre-check in the page-action family's shared injector and in `captureTabScreenshot`; keep the catch at `:946` as a backstop that maps the "Cannot access contents" message to the same denial shape); `extension/lib/permission-approval*.js` / the grant path behind the card (the Allow handler must call `chrome.permissions.request({origins})` on the click — verify it already does for `grantOrigins` and add it if it only handles `permissions`); `extension/ntp/ntp.js` (nothing if the card path is shared); tests.
  - Steps: (1) unit RED-first: `tests/browser-tools-read-page.test.ts` (new or nearest) with a fake `chrome.permissions.contains` returning false → `readPage` returns the denial shape with `grantOrigins:["https://example.com"]`; with the raw executeScript rejection → the same shape (backstop). (2) Implement. (3) Journey: seeded profile WITHOUT host access for the fixture origin; scripted provider calls `read_page` → the Allow card names the site; click Allow (the harness pre-grants via `test-manifest-pregranted` the way `scripts/webmcp-acceptance.ts:54` documents, since headless cannot show the native prompt) → the run resumes and the transcript contains the page text; click Deny in a second run → the card shows the declined line and the model's final text mentions the site could not be read. (4) Screenshot `read-page-allow-card.png`, `read-page-denied.png`.
  - Out of scope: `list_tabs` (needs only `tabs`); WebMCP tool calls (their own consent path); making host access install-time again (rejected by HOST-ACCESS-STORY-01).
- Review: pending
- Gates: the falsification gates apply

  - Browser: the two journey checks in Steps (3) in `EXPECTED`; the named screenshots.
  - Full suite: `npm run build && deno test -A tests/ && deno run -A scripts/chrome-journeys.ts` green.
  - Constraints: one Allow card per origin per run; the grant is requested on the owner's click only (a user gesture — never pre-emptively); the card copy names the site and the reason; no emoji; fail closed on privileged URLs.

- Next: the `readPage` pre-check + unit test, then confirm the card's Allow handler requests origins.

title: [CAP-FB-20260901-RUN-BUDGET-EVERY-ITEM-01] A run stops after four to six tool actions — the lazy protocol charges two steps per action, selection refs are single-use, and the budget is invisible
description:
## [CAP-FB-20260901-RUN-BUDGET-EVERY-ITEM-01] A run stops after four to six tool actions — the lazy protocol charges two steps per action, selection refs are single-use, and the budget is invisible
- Feedback: 2026-09-01 — owner, same 30-tab research run: "it certainly doesn't go through all of them", "whatever is happening ends too early, it should go through every tab", "I get a lot of selection-replayed errors and I've no idea what it means", "list_tabs, I'm not sure it gets all the tabs". The run log shows 8 `execute_tool` calls (two of them `selection-replayed`), 6 `search_tools` calls, and a digest written after reading two pages.
- Updated: 2026-09-01 22:23 UTC
- Status: OPEN
- Resume: —
- Priority: P0
- Owner: model worker (Fable 5 subagent) under the reanalysis coordinator session — CLAIMED; do not start a parallel attempt
- Workspace: active (local path private)
- Branch: `cap/run-budget-every-item` (pushed to origin as the candidate branch; merged by the coordinator)
- Base: `ffaac6af`
- Candidate: —
- Shipping: —
- Acceptance: With 30 open tabs and "read every tab and produce a sourced digest", a run on gemini-3.7-flash reads every readable tab (one `read_page` per tab, no `selection-replayed`, no repeated `search_tools` for a tool it already holds) and the digest cites every readable tab; the conversation shows a step counter ("Step 34 of 80") while working and, if the budget is exhausted, a "Budget reached — Continue" card that resumes the same thread with the same context rather than a silent finish. Protocol errors the model or owner can see are sentences with a next action, never a bare token like `selection-replayed`.
  - Context: three compounding causes. (1) Budget: `extension/lib/agent.js:536` `maxIterations = 12` (the hub default — `service-worker.js:2457` passes 12 when unset; named agents `routes/agent-worker.js:196` same default, capped 64) and `agent.js:947` `innerStepLimit: Math.max(2, Math.min(maxIterations, 8))` — one inner turn is at most 8 model steps, and the lazy protocol costs TWO model steps per logical tool action (`search_tools` then `execute_tool`; the comment at 944-946 says so), so a turn fits ~4 tool actions. (2) Single-use refs: `extension/lib/tool-selection.js:271-290` `claim` deletes the record on first use and any reuse is `selection-replayed` (`:243`); `release` (`:298`) hands it back ONLY on argument-validation failure (`lazy-tool-protocol.js:852-857`), not on a tool-level failure (the owner's log: `execute_tool:5` failed with "No tab with id", the model retried the same ref at `:7` → replayed). A ref authorizes nothing (`authorizes:false, requiresLiveAuthorization:true` at `:198-200`, and `authorizeRecord` runs live per call at `lazy-tool-protocol.js:863`), so single-use buys no security — it only forces a `search_tools` round-trip before EVERY call and doubles the step cost. `TOOL_SELECTION_BOUNDS.maxSelectionsPerRun: 32` (`tool-selection.js:13`) is a further hard ceiling of 32 tool actions per run. (3) Opaque errors: `selection-replayed`, `selection-missing-or-expired`, `selection-scope-mismatch`, `selection-catalog-stale`, `selection-source-stale` (`tool-selection.js:239-260`) reach the model and the card as bare tokens. What must NOT change: live authorization per call; the run-bound scope check (`sameContext`); the catalog-generation staleness check; the per-run ceilings stay bounded (raise, do not remove); the fence on untrusted results.
  - Reproduce today: open 30 tabs (any), run "Read every open tab and produce a sourced digest" on a real provider; count `execute_tool` rows in the run log (≤ 8) and `selection-replayed` rows (≥ 1 whenever a tool call fails and the model retries); observe the run finishes with a digest that cites 2-3 tabs and no UI element says why it stopped.
  - Files: `extension/lib/tool-selection.js` (a ref is REUSABLE for the same tool within its run until `expiresAt`: replace the delete-on-claim with a per-ref `uses` counter bounded by a new `maxUsesPerSelection: 64`; keep `#consumed` for refs that hit the bound so the error stays honest; `defaultTtlMs` 60 s → 10 min (a 30-tab loop takes longer than a minute), `maxTtlMs` 15 min; `maxSelectionsPerRun` 32 → 128; every error token gains a `message` sibling in plain English with the next action, e.g. `selection-replayed` → "This selection reference has been used 64 times; call search_tools once more for a fresh one"); `extension/lib/lazy-tool-protocol.js` (release the claim on a tool-level failure as well as on validation failure, so a failed call never burns the ref; surface `message` in the error result the model sees); `extension/lib/agent.js` (`maxIterations` default 12 → 48 for interactive hub runs, `innerStepLimit` → `Math.max(2, Math.min(maxIterations, 24))`; emit `{type:"budget", step, total}` progress so the UI can count); `extension/background/service-worker.js` (the run's step budget as a run-log field; when exhausted, the terminal carries `errorCategory:"budget"` with `errorAction:"Continue"` — the thread's existing terminal/action wiring renders it; a `run.continue` route resumes the thread with the same executionId lineage (the durable resume path already exists — reuse it)); `extension/lib/master-skill.js` (the operating manual: "A selection reference works for every call of that tool for the rest of the run — do not search again for a tool you already hold"; "When asked for every item, iterate every item; say which items you could not read and why"); `extension/shared/components.js` (`<conversation-run-status>` shows "Step N of M"; the budget card reuses the approval-card chrome with one Continue button); `extension/lib/browser-tools.js` (`list_tabs` 2202: add `windowId`, `groupId`, `active`, `index`, and a `count` field so the model and the owner can verify completeness; verify `chrome.tabs.query({})` spans every window — record the count in the History line); tests.
  - Steps: (1) unit RED-first: `tests/tool-selection.test.ts` — "a ref resolves for a second execute of the same tool", "the 65th use is selection-replayed with a message", "a tool-level failure releases the ref"; `tests/lazy-tool-protocol*.test.ts` — the error result carries `message`. (2) Implement the reusable ref + release-on-failure + messages. (3) Budget: raise defaults, emit the budget event, terminal `errorCategory:"budget"` + Continue. (4) Manual text. (5) `list_tabs` completeness fields. (6) Journey (scripted provider): a 12-tab fixture, the demo model iterates 12 `read_page` calls with ONE `search_tools` → 12 `execute_tool` rows, 0 replayed; a run whose budget is 4 → the Continue card renders and clicking it produces a second execution on the same thread. (7) Live check on gemini-3.7-flash with 30 real tabs (keys in ~/.env; never log them): every readable tab read; record counts.
  - Out of scope: the host-permission denial on `read_page` (CAP-FB-20260901-READ-PAGE-HOST-GRANT-01); provider-side context limits (a 30-page context on a small model may need summarisation — record it as a finding, do not solve it here); the pipeline lane (TOOL-PIPELINES-01) which is the structural fix for loops.
- Review: pending
- Gates: the falsification gates apply
  - Unit: as Steps (1). Falsification: revert the reusable-ref change → "a ref resolves for a second execute" RED → restore → GREEN; revert release-on-failure → its test RED → restore → GREEN.
  - Browser: the two journey checks in Steps (6) added to `EXPECTED`; screenshots `run-budget-step-counter.png`, `run-budget-continue-card.png`, `every-tab-digest.png` (the live 30-tab run's transcript, tabs count visible).
  - Full suite: `npm run build && deno test -A tests/ && deno run -A scripts/chrome-journeys.ts` green; `deno run -A scripts/security-injection*.ts` (the fence probe) still green since results stay fenced.
  - Constraints: every bound stays finite and named in `TOOL_SELECTION_BOUNDS` / `LAZY_TOOL_PROTOCOL_BOUNDS`; no authorization is cached across calls; the manual stays under its byte budget (MODEL-CALL-ECONOMY-01 measures it — add no more than 300 bytes); no eval.
- Blockers: —
- Next: the reusable ref + release-on-failure first (removes half the steps and every `selection-replayed` in the owner's log), then the budget/Continue.
- Recover: `git log --oneline --all --grep=CAP-FB-20260901-RUN-BUDGET-EVERY-ITEM-01`
- History:
  - 2026-09-01 20:30 UTC — opened from the owner's run log. Verified at `origin/main@ffaac6af`: `agent.js:536/947` (12 iterations, 8 inner steps), `tool-selection.js:13/243/271-290/298` (32 selections, delete-on-claim, release only on validation failure), `lazy-tool-protocol.js:852-857`.
  - 2026-09-01 22:23 UTC — CLAIMED by the reanalysis coordinator; worker started in its own worktree on `cap/run-budget-every-item` off `origin/main@ffaac6af`. Other agents: pick a different entry.

title: [CAP-FB-20260901-APPROVAL-RESUME-REEXECUTES-01] After the owner clicks Allow, the paused tool call is not re-run — the model is told to "retry with a fresh search_tools selection" and the string leaks into the transcript
description:
## [CAP-FB-20260901-APPROVAL-RESUME-REEXECUTES-01] After the owner clicks Allow, the paused tool call is not re-run — the model is told to "retry with a fresh search_tools selection" and the string leaks into the transcript
- Feedback: 2026-09-01 — found by the EXEC-DEMO-01 rehearsal (worker, headed and headless): after Allow on the in-chat browser-control card, the resumed run's `group_tabs` card reads "Error: Owner approved the requested capability, but this attempt did not run. Retry group_tabs now with a fresh search_tools selection." The `demo-path: step 1` journey check is red on exactly this (forbidden string `search_tools` in the thread); the sibling `create_asset` call issued alongside the paused call fails on resume with a raw `selection-scope-mismatch` card and the artifact is dropped.
- Updated: 2026-09-01 23:00 UTC
- Status: OPEN
- Resume: —
- Priority: P0
- Owner: model worker (Fable 5 subagent) under the reanalysis coordinator session — CLAIMED; do not start a parallel attempt
- Workspace: active (local path private)
- Branch: `cap/approval-resume-reexecutes` (pushed to origin as the candidate branch; merged by the coordinator)
- Base: `a52315fa`
- Candidate: —
- Shipping: —
- Acceptance: When the owner approves a permission card, the paused tool call is executed by the runtime with its ORIGINAL arguments and the model receives that tool's real result as if the call had succeeded first time — no "retry" instruction, no second `search_tools`, no `search_tools`/`selection-*` string anywhere in the transcript. Sibling tool calls issued in the same model step are not invalidated by the pause (they run, or are re-run, under the same run scope). Deny and expiry keep their current terminal sentences. The card shows the tool's real outcome (e.g. "Grouped 3 tabs into Web Development"). `demo-path: step 1` goes green.
  - Context: `extension/lib/agent.js:1051-1071` — `onPostToolUse` awaits `onPermissionRequest(permissionDenial)`; on `approved` it rewrites `modelContent` to the retry sentence (`:1061`) and `userSummary` to "BLOCKED — approved; retry required" (`:1066`) instead of re-dispatching. The comment at `:1055-1057` explains why: the lazy protocol's grant digest changed while the call was paused, so the OLD selectionRef no longer resolves (`extension/lib/lazy-tool-protocol.js` `authorizeRecord` "before-validation"/"after-validation" and the catalog-generation check in `extension/lib/tool-selection.js:250`). The fix is to re-execute inside the runtime: after `approved`, call the same executor the loop uses (`executeWorkerTool` in `extension/background/service-worker.js` for hub runs, or the lazy protocol's `execute` with a runtime-issued fresh selection for the SAME stableId + the ORIGINAL validated args) and put THAT result into `e.result` — the model never learns a pause happened. The sibling failure: a second tool call in the same step resolves its ref after the generation bump → `selection-scope-mismatch`; with the re-execution path the runtime must re-issue refs for in-flight calls of the same step (or CAP-FB-20260901-RUN-BUDGET-EVERY-ITEM-01's reusable refs must survive a generation bump when the descriptor's stableId is unchanged — coordinate: land whichever comes first, keep both). What must NOT change: the approval binds the digest of the exact requested capability; a denied/expired call is never executed; the re-execution runs under the SAME run fence, grant lock and untrusted fence as any tool call; one card per distinct requirement.
  - Reproduce today: `deno run -A scripts/chrome-journeys.ts` at `origin/cap/exec-demo@b6898cba` → `demo-path: step 1 groups tabs and renders sentences` prints `forbidden=["search_tools"]` and FAILS; headed: fresh profile, real model, "Group my open tabs by topic…", click Allow → the `group_tabs` card shows the retry sentence, the model calls `search_tools` again, and the artifact from the parallel `create_asset` is lost.
  - Files: `extension/lib/agent.js` (`onPostToolUse` ~1051: on `approved`, re-execute and replace `e.result` with the real result; keep `permissionRequirement`/`permissionDecision` on the progress event so the card still records the grant; add a `reexecuted:true` marker on the event for the card's "approved, then ran" line); `extension/lib/lazy-tool-protocol.js` (a runtime-only `reexecute({stableId, args, context})` that issues its own selection, bypassing the model-facing search; scoped so a page/model principal can never call it); `extension/background/service-worker.js` (thread the re-execute dispatcher into `createAgent` like `onPermissionRequest`); `extension/shared/components.js` (the tool card: status `done` with a small "approved by you, then ran" caption — no new component); `tests/agent-permission-resume.test.ts` (new); the `demo-path` group already on `cap/exec-demo` is the browser gate.
  - Steps: (1) unit RED-first with a fake tool that returns `permissionDenial` once then succeeds: "approved → the event's result is the tool's real result and modelContent contains neither `search_tools` nor `Retry`", "denied → unchanged terminal sentence", "a sibling call in the same step still completes". description:
## [CAP-FB-20260901-TOOL-RESULT-FULL-JSON-01] Tool results are cut to 300 characters at the source, so the card, the run log and the reopened thread can never show what a tool returned
- Feedback: 2026-09-01 — owner, using the agent view on a real 30-tab research run ("Collect every article on my open tabs…"): "I can't see the results of the tool call. It is critical we have a nice JSON formatted result", "it errors on a tool call and I can't see the error in the UI", "when we reload a lot of the transcript is lost and I can't expand the UI of the final results". The exported run log confirms every `tool-result` row's `result` string ends in `…` at ~300 characters.
- Updated: 2026-09-01 22:23 UTC
- Status: OPEN
- Resume: —
- Priority: P0
- Owner: model worker (Fable 5 subagent) under the reanalysis coordinator session — CLAIMED; do not start a parallel attempt
- Workspace: active (local path private)
- Branch: `cap/tool-result-full-json` (pushed to origin as the candidate branch; merged by the coordinator)
- Base: `ffaac6af`
- Candidate: —
- Shipping: —
- Acceptance: A tool card in the live run AND in the reopened thread shows (a) a one-line human summary, (b) an expandable, syntax-highlighted, pretty-printed JSON tree of the COMPLETE bounded result (the same bytes the model received, redacted), (c) a Copy button that copies the full pretty JSON, (d) for a failed call, the error text as the card headline in the error colour — including an error nested inside a lazy-protocol `ok:true` envelope (`{"ok":true,"selectedTool":"read_page","result":{"error":"…"}}`) and a bare protocol error (`{"ok":false,"error":"selection-replayed"}`), never a success-looking card. The full result survives a reload of the agent view and a service-worker restart. Results are bounded at 64 KiB per row (the lazy protocol's own `maxResultBytes`) with the never-silent truncation marker, and the run log stays under the retention cap.
  - Context: `extension/lib/agent.js:516` `summarizeToolResult(result)` slices every result to 300 chars BEFORE it is emitted as the `tool-result` progress event (`agent.js:1085-1094`). The service worker persists exactly that string (`extension/background/service-worker.js:2690` — `result` comes from `event.result`) into the journal and the durable run log (`durableRuns.appendLog`). The cards read the same string back: `extension/ntp/ntp.js:2259` `renderAgentHistory` → `container.appendTool({result: summary, detail: raw})` where `raw` is the persisted 300-char string; `extension/shared/components.js:4727` reads `tool-detail` and renders the "bounded collapsible tree" into a `<pre>` with `max-height:180px` (`components.js:4658`). So the 300-char cut happens once at the source and every surface downstream is faithful to a stub. The terminal (final answer) path was just fixed the same way by `CAP-FB-20260831-TASK-VIEW-FULL-RESPONSE-01` (`origin/main@ffaac6af`): the full text is stored as a retained payload (`retainedPayloadRef`) with byte-aware caps (`extension/lib/durable-runs.js` `boundedBytes`, the 252 KiB cap and the `…(response truncated to N KiB…)` marker) and a Show-full-response expander with Copy. This entry applies the same pattern to tool results. What must NOT change: redaction — every reader routes through `extension/lib/tool-summary.js` `redactToolResult` (secret-shaped keys + credential shapes in string leaves) and the write path redacts before persisting; the untrusted fence markers (`<<<UNTRUSTED run:…>>>`) stay in the stored bytes; nothing renders through innerHTML — the tree is built with textContent (the existing renderer already does; keep it).
  - Reproduce today: (1) any run that calls `read_page` on a long page; (2) open the tool card → the detail ends mid-JSON with `…`; (3) Settings → Developer → export the run log (or `agent.runs.get`) → every `tool-result.result` is ≤ 301 chars; (4) a `read_page` on an ungranted host produces `{"ok":true,…"result":{"error":"Cannot access contents of the page…"}}` with the row's `ok:false`, and the card shows a done/neutral state rather than the error headline (verify with a screenshot — if `toolResultSignalsError` at `components.js:4736` does catch it, record that and keep only the bare-string case); (5) `{"ok":false,"error":"selection-replayed"}` renders as the literal string with no explanation.
  - Files: `extension/lib/agent.js` (`summarizeToolResult` 516 → emit BOTH `result` (the 300-char summary, unchanged, for list surfaces) and `resultFull` (the redacted JSON-serialised full result, bounded to 64 KiB via a byte-aware cut with the marker)); `extension/background/service-worker.js` (2690: persist `resultFull` on the row as a retained payload the same way the terminal does — `durableRuns.appendLog` with a `payloadRef` and `retainedPayloadRef`; keep the journal (`journalAppend`) row small — the journal is the list surface); `extension/lib/durable-runs.js` (a `tool-result` payload store keyed `run-payload:<executionId>:tool:<callId>` under the existing per-run byte budget; compaction (`compactExecution`) keeps the payloads of the thread's visible rows — coordinate with CAP-FB-20260901-THREAD-RELOAD-FIDELITY-01); `extension/ntp/ntp.js` (`renderAgentHistory` 2259: `detail` = the full payload when present, falling back to the row's `result`); `extension/shared/components.js` (the tool card ~4700-4900: a `<tool-result-json>` region — pretty-printed JSON via `JSON.stringify(v, null, 2)` into a tree with collapsible objects/arrays, key/string/number/boolean/null token classes using the theme tokens, `max-height` raised to a scrollable 360px with a "Show all" toggle, a Copy button (`navigator.clipboard.writeText` of the full pretty JSON), and the error headline rule: if the row is `ok:false`, or the unwrapped result has a string `error`, or the envelope is `ok:false` — headline = that error text, status = error); `docs/components.html` (gallery specimens: success with nested JSON, nested-error, bare protocol error, 64 KiB truncated); `extension/lib/tool-summary.js` (a `toolResultErrorText(raw)` helper used by both the card and the summary line); tests.
  - Steps: (1) unit: `tests/tool-summary.test.ts` — `toolResultErrorText` returns the nested error for the three shapes; `tests/agent-progress-events.test.ts` (or nearest) — the `tool-result` event carries `resultFull` ≤ 64 KiB with the marker when the raw result is 200 KiB, and never carries an unredacted `sk-…` leaf. (2) SW: persist the payload; `tests/durable-runs*.test.ts` — the payload is readable back by `run-payload:` ref after `forgetCachedState()`; compaction keeps it for the visible rows. (3) Card: build the tree renderer + Copy + error headline in `components.js`; sync the gallery (`npm run check:gallery`). (4) `renderAgentHistory` reads the payload. (5) Journey: a scripted-provider run whose tool returns a 5 KiB object → the card's expanded tree shows a leaf that lies beyond byte 300; a nested-error result → the headline is the error text in the error colour; reload the agent view → both still true.

Screenshots `tool-result-json-tree.png`, `tool-result-nested-error.png`, `tool-result-after-reload.png`.

title: [CAP-FB-20260828-TOOL-RESULT-ENVELOPE-01] The lazy protocol envelope leaks into the transcript and erases results
description:
## [CAP-FB-20260828-TOOL-RESULT-ENVELOPE-01] The lazy protocol envelope leaks into the transcript and erases results
- Feedback: 2026-08-28 — product owner pasted a live run: `{"selectionRef":"sel_ba138fff…","arguments":{"content":"<!DOCTYPE html>…"}}` and `{"modelContent":"{\"ok\":true,\"selectedTool\":\"create_asset\",\"result\":{\"bounded\":true,\"summary\":\"tool completed; result was not safely serializable\"}…"}` — "it should be showing the asset inline. The result of tool calls is never rendered correctly, and even the inputs aren't formatted well"
- Updated: 2026-08-28 07:10 UTC
- Status: DONE
- Priority: P0
- Owner: claude-opus-5 implementer session
- Workspace: active (local path private)
- Branch: working tree on `origin/main`
- Base: `88ed2df2`
- Candidate: this commit
- Shipping: —
- Acceptance: a transcript names the tool that actually RAN and shows the arguments it actually received, never `execute_tool` with a `selectionRef`; a `create_asset` renders its artifact card inline; and a result that trips a protocol bound keeps its identifying fields instead of being replaced wholesale by a summary string
- Review: author review with the falsification gates; tested against the exact payload the owner pasted
- Gates: unit **1815/0** · build clean
- Blockers: —
- Next: the tool card's own presentation (collapsed head, JSON view) is `CAP-FB-20260827-TOOL-CALL-LEGIBILITY-01`; this entry only makes the card show the RIGHT tool and the RIGHT data
- Recover: `git grep -n "effectiveToolCall\|degradeResult" -- extension/shared/conversation.js extension/lib/lazy-tool-protocol.js`
- History:
  - 2026-08-28 — DONE at `origin/main@dc04e4c7`. Merged and green.
  - 2026-08-28 07:10 UTC — **three defects, one root cause: the lazy protocol envelope was treated as the result.** Since the lazy cutover every run gets only `search_tools`/`execute_tool`, so the tool NAME the UI sees is `execute_tool` and the real tool is named inside the payload. **(1) Results were being ERASED, not bounded.** `asset.create` returned `index: res.index` — the ENTIRE artifact index — to the model on every create. Measured: at ~72 artifacts that alone exceeds the protocol's 512-node result bound; `projectData` THROWS on the bound, and `projectResult` caught every throw and replaced the whole result with `{bounded:true, summary:"…not safely serializable"}`. So past ~72 artifacts the model never learned the id of the thing it had just made, and the UI had nothing to render. **My own artifact-library change made this worse** — one shared index instead of per-origin reaches the bound sooner. Fixed at the source (`asset.create` returns identity: id/name/type/origin/size, never the index and never the content back) and defensively (`degradeResult` keeps top-level scalars and says how many fields were dropped, instead of erasing). **(2) The card named the envelope, not the tool** — `effectiveToolCall` now resolves `execute_tool` to its `selectedTool` and unwraps the arguments from under `arguments`, dropping the meaningless `selectionRef`; the live path corrects the header once the result names the tool, and the replay path resolves it from the pair. **(3) My in-thread artifact work from an hour earlier NEVER FIRED in a real run** — `artifactFromToolResult` keyed on the tool name being `create_asset`, which under the lazy protocol it never is. It now unwraps the envelope first. That bug was invisible to its own tests because they exercised the direct-dispatch shape; the new tests use the exact payload the owner pasted.

title: [CAP-FB-20260828-ARTIFACTS-IN-THREAD-01] Artifacts render in the thread that produced them
description:
## [CAP-FB-20260828-ARTIFACTS-IN-THREAD-01] Artifacts render in the thread that produced them
- Feedback: 2026-08-28 — product owner: "assets created by an agent should also be easily visible in the chat/task/agent log so they can be viewed in the context in which they are created. I never see assets there and they should be (as well as globally visible)"
- Updated: 2026-08-28 05:30 UTC
- Status: DONE
- Priority: P0
- Owner: claude-opus-5 implementer session
- Workspace: active (local path private)
- Branch: working tree on `origin/main`
- Base: `2fc8bc1b`
- Candidate: this commit
- Shipping: —
- Acceptance: a run that produces an artifact shows it in the conversation as a real, openable card — name, type, size, provenance — not as an opaque `create_asset · done` row; the card is there LIVE as the run streams and still there when the thread is reopened; and it renders through the same `<artifact-card>` the library uses rather than a thread-only duplicate
- Review: author review with the falsification gates (AGENTS.md, "Review without a second model"); rendered and screenshotted in a real loaded extension
- Gates: unit **1811/0** (10 new) · Chrome journeys **127/127** · component gallery smoke **35/35** · gallery drift clean · build clean · visual verification in headless Chrome at 1440×1600
- Blockers: —
- Next: the preview panel shows a type placeholder rather than the artifact's content, because the thread does not set `card.preview`. The library loads previews for its newest N; doing the same in-thread is a small follow-up, not a blocker
- Recover: `git grep -n "artifactFromToolResult" -- extension/shared/conversation.js`
- History:
  - 2026-08-28 — DONE at `origin/main@dc04e4c7`. Merged and green.
  - 2026-08-28 05:30 UTC — **implemented.** Before this, a run that made something rendered as `create_asset · done · 31ms` and the artifact itself was invisible; for a non-HTML artifact there was no trace of it in the conversation at all. (An HTML artifact did get a live sandboxed preview, but with no name, no identity and no way to open it.) The fix is one PURE derivation, `artifactFromToolResult(toolName, result)`, used by BOTH paths: the live event stream calls it on each tool result, and `toolRowsFromRunLog` emits an `artifact` row straight after the tool row that produced it. Sharing one derivation is the point — an artifact cannot appear while a run streams and then vanish when the thread is reopened, because there is no second implementation to disagree. It accepts the object form (live) and the JSON-string form (replayed logs) and returns identical output for both, which is asserted. A failed create renders nothing: telling the owner they have something they do not is worse than silence.
  - 2026-08-28 05:30 UTC — reuses the SAME `<artifact-card>` as the library rather than a thread-only rendering, per the project's anti-hand-roll rule — a second artifact card is exactly the duplication that produced the toggle and menu bugs. Events bubble, so the hub wires open / open-tab once by delegation and every card, live or replayed, behaves identically.
  - 2026-08-28 05:30 UTC — **caught in visual verification, not in the tests:** the first render showed a **Delete** button that nothing in the thread wired, so it did nothing. A control that does nothing is the same defect class as one that claims a success it never checked. Added an optional `actions` allowlist to `<artifact-card>` (omitted keeps every action, so the library is untouched); the thread declares `actions="open-tab reuse"`. An artifact is also not something you delete from the transcript that records making it — deletion belongs in the library.

- Base: `e2442e90`
- Candidate: working tree — one shared library, provenance filtering, migration, gallery wired
- Shipping: —
- Acceptance: an artifact survives the deletion of the agent that made it and of the task it was made in. Deleting a Site Agent still clears that site's MEMORY and enrollment, and still removes its scripts and host permission, but it does not destroy the owner's artifacts. Existing artifacts already sitting in site stores are migrated, not orphaned or dropped. The artifact keeps its provenance — which agent, which thread, which run made it — so the thread view can still show it and so a deleted agent's artifacts are still attributable. `asset.delete` remains the ONLY way an artifact goes away, and stays an owner-direct action. A regression test deletes a Site Agent that has artifacts and asserts they are still listed and readable afterwards
- Review: fresh-session review; falsification — the regression test must be shown FAILING against current `main`, where the artifacts genuinely disappear
- Gates: full unit suite; Chrome journeys green; `npm run test:opfs` real-browser OPFS verification; the security suite (this moves data across store boundaries, so origin-keying must be re-argued, not assumed)
- Blockers: —
- Next: decide the target layout first — the safest shape is that ALL artifacts live in the master store with an origin/agent/thread provenance field, since `assetStore("master")` is already the master memory and the per-origin split is what creates the coupling
- Recover: `git grep -n "function assetStore" -- extension/lib/artifacts.js && git grep -n "siteMemory(canonical).clear()" -- extension/background/service-worker.js`
- History:
  - 2026-08-28 — DONE at `origin/main@dc04e4c7`. Merged and green.
  - 2026-08-28 04:30 UTC — **fixed; red-then-green proven.** `tests/artifact-durability.test.ts` was written FIRST and shown failing against unmodified main with "the artifact must still be readable after the site store is cleared" — the data loss is real, not inferred. **The bug was bigger than filed:** the gallery only ever listed `origin:"master"`, so a site-origin artifact was never visible in the library in the first place, and then `agent.delete` destroyed it. **Fix:** `assetStore()` always returns the master store, so the library is ONE store and `origin` is purely the provenance it already carried on every row. `listAssets(origin)` filters by provenance; a new `listAllAssets()` is the library view and `asset.list` with no origin (or `"all"`) returns it; the gallery now asks for that. `migrateSiteAssetsToLibrary(origin)` moves pre-existing site-store artifacts across — body before index, verify the copy is readable before removing the original, idempotent — and both site-store clear paths call it BEFORE clearing, so no profile loses anything. **Not a boundary change:** scoped (site/hook) runs get no management tools at all (`scoped ? {} : managementToolset(...)`), so no site agent could read another origin's artifacts before or after. **Two things the tests caught in my own change:** the per-origin count cap was being counted against the whole shared index, which starved every origin after the first (restored to counting that origin's rows); and the index byte bound had been per-origin, so leaving it at 128 KiB after sharing the index was a capacity regression — raised to 2 MiB (~940 rows to ~15,000). The remaining silent-eviction behaviour is `CAP-FB-20260828-ARTIFACT-LIBRARY-CAPACITY-01`, filed rather than folded in. Gates: unit 1801/0, Chrome journeys 127/127, security PASS, `npm run test:opfs` 6/6.
  - 2026-08-28 02:40 UTC — found by tracing the owner's requirement through the code rather than assuming. `assetStore(origin)` in `extension/lib/artifacts.js` returns `masterMemory()` for `"master"` and **`siteMemory(origin)` for anything else**. The `create_asset` tool takes an `origin` argument and its own description invites the model to use one ("Use origin 'master' for a hub-level artifact, or an origin for a site-specific one"), so artifacts genuinely land in site stores. `agent.delete` calls **`siteMemory(canonical).clear()`** as part of its cleanup. So deleting a Site Agent permanently destroys every artifact created under that origin — exactly the case the owner says the artifact library exists to protect against. This is data loss, not a UI issue, which is why it is P0 ahead of the presentation work.
  - 2026-08-28 02:40 UTC — checked and NOT affected: `deleteNamedAgent` clears `namedAgentMemory(slug)`, which is a different store from `assetStore`, so deleting a NAMED agent does not take master artifacts with it. The exposure is the site-origin path only. Thread/task deletion also does not currently touch assets.

title: [CAP-FB-20260827-THREAD-OPEN-SEQUENTIAL-READS-01] Thread open serializes 25 OPFS reads before first paint
description:
## [CAP-FB-20260827-THREAD-OPEN-SEQUENTIAL-READS-01] Thread open serializes 25 OPFS reads before first paint
- Feedback: 2026-08-27 — product owner: "Loading tasks is quite slow"
- Updated: 2026-08-27 23:30 UTC
- Status: DONE
- Priority: P0
- Owner: unassigned
- Workspace: none
- Branch: none
- Base: `139b6f92`
- Candidate: this commit — stages 1 and 2 of the design implemented and measured; stage 3 (chunked storage) not started
- Shipping: —
- Acceptance: opening a thread with a full 25-execution history paints its first screen in well under a second on a cold service worker, measured in a real loaded extension with a seeded profile — and the measurement harness is committed so the number cannot silently regress. The per-execution log reads run concurrently rather than one after another; `thread.get` does not have to assemble every execution before the surface can render anything; and the honest truncation markers (`truncatedExecutions`, `truncatedLogs`, `logFailed`) are all preserved
- Review: independent review by a different model/session; before/after timings from a real loaded extension, not a unit benchmark
- Gates: full unit suite; Chrome journeys green; `tests/thread-run-view.test.ts` still green including the reconciliation and degraded-read paths
- Blockers: —
- Next: BATCH the appends. Stage 3 is landed and wired; writes are 12x faster but still one file-open PER ROW because `appendLog` is called a row at a time. Buffering within a tick and flushing once is the remaining win — a change to WHEN we write, not how it is stored, and `appendRecords` already takes an array. Superseded note: stage 3 WIRING. The primitive is landed and green; wiring it into durableRuns hit an UNEXPLAINED row-composition difference (below) and was reverted rather than forced. Resolve that first: instrument what the 126 non-tool rows in a 250-row window actually are, and decide deliberately whether the cap should keep rows in true APPEND order (the WAL) or in `(at, idempotencyKey)` order (today). That is a semantic choice about the durable run authority, not a test to bend. Original note: a WAL rather than chunking — one append-only JSONL file per execution, no index file, byte-range tail reads. The idempotency gate that blocked the chunking design is GONE (the key is a field on every record and a tail scan is 0.4 ms). The remaining care is the partial-first-line boundary on a sliced read, single-writer discipline, and an explicit retention bound
- Recover: `git grep -n "for (const e of viewedExecutions)" -- extension/lib/thread-run-view.js`
- History:
  - 2026-08-28 — DONE at `origin/main@dc04e4c7`. Task open 918 ms → 27 ms (~34x) and writing 1,000 log rows 171,375 ms → 1,390 ms (~123x), measured by the committed `scripts/thread-open-trace.ts`. Merged and the journey suite green at that tip (127/127, three consecutive runs).
  - 2026-08-28 15:30 UTC — **stage 3 (the WAL) is LANDED AND WIRED. Task open 918 ms → 146 ms (6.3x); writing 1,000 rows 171 s → 14 s (12x).** Full matrix: open 15/213/918 ms → 9/40/146 ms at 10/250/1,000 rows; write 140 ms/11.2 s/171 s → 70 ms/2.0 s/14.1 s. Gates: unit **1892/0**, Chrome journeys **127/127**, `npm run test:opfs` **6/6**, security suite **PASS**, build clean.
  - 2026-08-28 15:30 UTC — **the earlier revert was right: every one of the failures was real, and three of the four were in MY code or MY test doubles.** (1) `migrateExecutionLog` deleted legacy rows with `store.remove?.()` — a method the durable store does not have, so optional chaining silently deleted NOTHING and migration re-ran on every append; the `accepted` row (written directly by `start()`, carrying no idempotencyKey) failed the dedup and was re-appended each time: **401 copies in an 802-row log**, which is exactly why a 250-row page held only 124 tool rows. Fixed with a run-once marker plus `compareAndDelete`. (2) `lockedRead` registered a reader as active BEFORE awaiting the write chain, so a concurrent migration waited on a reader that was waiting on it — a **deadlock** under the bounded-concurrency execution reads. A reader now takes its slot only once it is actually running. (3) The registry reached past its injected `store` straight to real OPFS; the log handle is now an injectable `logHandleFor` dependency, exactly as `store` already was, with one shared in-memory implementation in `extension/lib/run-log-wal-memory.js` rather than a third hand-rolled copy. (4) A hand-rolled writable double had no `seek`, so the WAL's seek-less fallback (which writes the FULL merged content) doubled the file on every append — that one looked like a product bug and was entirely the fake's.
  - 2026-08-28 15:30 UTC — coverage was rewritten, not dropped: the two `thread-log index:` tests asserted on the `run-log-idx:` mechanism the WAL replaces, so they now assert the same PROPERTIES against the log — cursor pagination reaching the oldest row (and, stronger than before, every row seen exactly once with no gaps or repeats), and a legacy key-value execution migrating into the log on first read with the legacy rows removed only after the log verifies. `FakeStore` also gained the real `keys()` and `compareAndDelete()` it had been missing, which is what had made a migration that never ran look like one that ran four times.
  - 2026-08-28 13:00 UTC — **stage 3 primitive LANDED (`0.2.344`); the wiring was attempted, hit something I could not explain, and was REVERTED rather than forced.** `extension/lib/run-log-wal.js` + 16 KATs are in and green. Wiring `appendLog`/`listLogs` onto it got as far as returning the right row COUNT (`listLogs` correctly returned 250 of 400 rows) but the projection produced **62 tool cards instead of 125**, because only 124 of those 250 rows were tool-call/tool-result — 126 were something else, and I could not account for them: the only three `appendLog` call sites in the product write tool-call, tool-result and task rows. The underlying difference is real and semantic: today the 250-row cap keeps rows sorted by `(at, idempotencyKey)`, whereas a WAL returns true APPEND order. Append order is arguably more correct, but which one the cap should keep is a decision about the durable run authority — the thing holding a user's task history — and I was not willing to change it by making a failing test agree with me.
  - 2026-08-28 13:00 UTC — kept from the attempt because each stands on its own: `durableRunLogHandle`/`removeDurableRunLog` in `memory.js` (the log lives INSIDE the execution's own directory, so everything that already removes an execution takes its log too); tolerant byte access in the WAL (`arrayBuffer`/`slice` when present, `text()` otherwise) plus a `seek`-less append fallback that is explicitly loud about being O(filesize) and test-only; and a mechanical fix to **20 test OPFS doubles** which all shared one copy-pasted `this.parts.push(String(chunk))` that corrupted any byte chunk into a comma-joined number string. Gates after the revert: unit **1892/0**, build clean.
  - 2026-08-28 11:30 UTC — **owner rejected the chunking design: "I don't want 1000 files. why not a WAL?" They were right, and by a larger margin than expected.** My chunking draft optimised WITHIN the existing key-value store instead of asking whether one KV record per row is the right primitive for what is literally an append-only event log. Probed the real storage facts in the actual extension service worker (`scripts/opfs-wal-probe.ts`, committed): `createSyncAccessHandle` is **unavailable** in the SW (only `createWritable`), but **append does not copy the file** — cost is flat at 1.8 / 0.7 / 0.5 / 0.5 / 0.6 ms as the file grows through 1, 250, 500, 750, 1,000 rows, which was the main risk in using `createWritable({keepExistingData:true})`. A 64 KiB `Blob.slice` tail read is **0.4 ms**; 1,000 rows written in one open is **1 ms**.
  - 2026-08-28 11:30 UTC — **measured comparison: writing 1,000 rows 171,000 ms → 1 ms batched (~600 ms even one-at-a-time); reading them 348 ms → 0.2-0.4 ms.** Roughly 1000x on reads and up to 170,000x on writes, against maybe 10x for chunking. Design rewritten in `docs/THREAD-LOADING-REDESIGN.md` section 3: one append-only JSONL file per execution, **no index file and no digest set** — the log IS the index, so the O(n^2) per-append index rewrite and the `recentDigests` set the chunking draft invented both simply stop existing. It is also SAFER: a torn write leaves an unterminated final line that the reader discards, where today a crash can leave an index entry naming a row file that was never written.
  - 2026-08-28 11:30 UTC — the idempotency gate that blocked stage 3 is dissolved rather than solved: the key is a field on every record and a tail scan costs 0.4 ms, so duplicate detection stops being a storage problem. New risks recorded honestly in section 5: the partial first line on a sliced tail read (the probe parsed 980 of 1,000 rows for exactly this reason), single-writer discipline (`createWritable` does not lock, so the SW must remain the only writer — this needs revisiting if logging ever moves into the agent workers), and retention, which is the one place the design ADDS a concern since a log grows without bound.
  - 2026-08-28 10:30 UTC — **stages 1 and 2 landed and measured: task open 918 ms → 348 ms at 1,000 log rows (2.6x); 213 → 72 ms at 250; 15 → 8 ms at 10.** Extrapolated to the product's own bound (6,250 rows), ~6 s → ~2.2 s. Stage 1 read a page's rows with bounded concurrency (32) and read executions with bounded concurrency (8) — they were serialised only because the loops awaited, and nothing about one execution's log depends on another's. Stage 2 replaced the single exclusive registry mutex with a read/write lock: readers share, writers stay fully exclusive against both readers and writers, so index/row atomicity, idempotency and recovery are untouched. `listLogs` had to be SPLIT for this, because its fallback path rebuilds and persists the row index and is therefore not a pure read: the shared path serves the indexed fast case, and a read that would have to rebuild returns a sentinel and is retried under the exclusive lock rather than writing underneath a concurrent writer.
  - 2026-08-28 10:30 UTC — **my stage-1 prediction was wrong, recorded rather than quietly dropped.** The design said stage 1 alone would reach 150-250 ms at 1,000 rows; it reached 425 ms. Reason: stage 1 made rows within a page concurrent, but every `listLogs` still queued on the one global mutex, so the bounded fan-out ACROSS executions could not actually overlap — that is cause (b), which stage 2 then addressed (425 → 348 ms). The model was right about the causes and wrong about how much stage 1 could deliver alone.
  - 2026-08-28 10:30 UTC — **also wrong, and corrected in the design: the "0 ms spans" finding.** The first draft claimed the product's per-stage instrumentation reported 0 ms and made fixing it part of the work. `cap-perf.js` was fine; the measuring harness read a field named `total` where `perfSummary` reports `totalMs`. With that fixed the attribution is unambiguous and confirms the model: at 1,000 rows `thread-view:logs` was 3,288 ms of the 3,384 ms in `thread.get:view` — **97% of task-open time** — while `thread-view:project` was 7 ms and `thread.get:read` 6 ms. The projection was never the problem.
  - 2026-08-28 10:30 UTC — the remaining cost is granularity, exactly as the design's section 2 said: 1,000 rows is still 1,000 OPFS file opens, and concurrency bounds the latency without reducing the syscall count. Gates: unit **1876/0** · Chrome journeys **127/127** · `npm run test:opfs` **6/6** · security suite PASS · build clean.
  - 2026-08-28 09:00 UTC — **measured, then designed.** `scripts/thread-open-trace.ts` (committed) seeds a real profile through the production `durableRuns.start`/`appendLog` and times the exact `thread.get` the UI calls — no provider and no API key, because task open is storage and projection, not inference. **Task open is linear at ~0.95 ms per log row:** 13 ms at 10 rows, 223 ms at 250, ~960 ms at 1,000. The product's own bound is 25 x 250 = 6,250 rows, which extrapolates to **~6 s** and matches the report. **The write path is worse and was not expected:** 14 ms/row at 10 rows, 45 ms at 250, **173 ms at 1,000** — writing 1,000 rows takes nearly three minutes, and seeding to the documented bound never finished. That is the live logging path, so a long task gets progressively slower AS IT RUNS, and because writes hold a global lock they also block opens.
  - 2026-08-28 09:00 UTC — four causes, all confirmed in source: (a) `appendLog` rewrites the ENTIRE per-execution row index on every append, so writing n rows costs O(n^2) index writes; (b) `locked()` is ONE global mutex over the whole registry, reads included, so nothing ever overlaps; (c) each log row is its own OPFS file, so a 250-row page is 250 sequential `store.get` calls; (d) three serialisations stack on open — `buildThreadRunView` awaits per execution, `listLogs` takes the mutex, `listLogs` awaits per row — about **6,300 sequential file reads** before `thread.get` returns anything, and it is all-or-nothing so there is no partial paint. The root cause is granularity: one file per row is the wrong unit for both reading and writing.
  - 2026-08-28 09:00 UTC — design in `docs/THREAD-LOADING-REDESIGN.md`: chunked append-only log pages (100 rows/file) with a small head record, a split lock (lock-free reads, per-execution writes), bounded-concurrency execution reads, and a streamed first page so first paint is a function of ONE page rather than of the thread. Staged so each step ships independently, highest value and lowest risk first. **Two claims in the first draft were wrong and are corrected in the doc:** `durable-quota.js` does not do byte accounting (it translates native QuotaExceededError), and `tests/thread-run-view.test.ts` does not exist — the projection is covered by `tests/thread-log-redesign.test.ts`. Also recorded honestly: the per-stage spans all report 0 ms in the production build, so stage attribution currently comes from reading the code, not from span data — fixing that instrumentation is part of the work, because a redesign justified by measurements needs its measurements to work.
  - 2026-08-27 23:30 UTC — captured from source inspection of the load path. `0.2.314` and `0.2.317` bounded the replay (25 executions × 250 log rows) and added per-run cursor pagination, which fixed the 10–15 s case. What remains is structural: `buildThreadRunView` reads those executions in a **sequential `for` loop with an `await` inside** (`extension/lib/thread-run-view.js`), so a full-history thread performs **25 serialized OPFS round-trips through the service worker — up to 6,250 log rows — before `thread.get` returns anything at all**. The reads are independent of each other; nothing requires them to be serial. `thread.get` is also all-or-nothing: the entire view is assembled before the surface receives a single message, so the "renders instantly" property from `0.2.317` applies within a run, not to opening the thread. Two further costs worth measuring at the same time: there is no cache, so re-opening the same thread pays the full price again, and the reconciliation pass can issue additional `commitTerminal` writes on the read path.

title: [CAP-FB-20260825-MAIN-GATES-RED-01] Main is red: Chrome journeys abort and two usage probes fail
description:
## [CAP-FB-20260825-MAIN-GATES-RED-01] Main is red: Chrome journeys abort and two usage probes fail
- Feedback: 2026-08-25 — an unrelated lane ran the full gates before landing and found three failures already on `origin/main`; both suites reproduce identically with all local work stashed
- Updated: 2026-08-25 17:10 UTC
- Status: DONE
- Resume: —
- Priority: P0
- Owner: claude-opus-5 implementer session
- Workspace: active (local path private)
- Branch: detached candidate on `origin/main`
- Base: `0626e6b`
- Candidate: this commit and its parent
- Shipping: —
- Acceptance: `deno run -A scripts/chrome-journeys.ts` reaches 126/126 again, and `tests/usage-authority.test.ts` PROBE-2 and PROBE-4 pass. Each failure is traced to the commit that introduced it and fixed there, or explicitly reclassified with evidence if the assertion — not the product — is what is wrong
- Review: author self-review 2026-08-25 (findings recorded in History and fixed); **no independent review** — the product owner asked the author to review directly
- Gates: Chrome journeys **127/127** (was 91/126 on untouched main); unit **1584/0**; security suite PASS; build, gallery drift, changelog and tasks-schema green. The regression test was verified to fail against the unfixed router with the exact production error
- Blockers: —
- Next: an independent pass on the durable key routing and thread-id validation if one becomes cheap; otherwise closed
- Recover: `deno run -A scripts/chrome-journeys.ts 2>&1 | tail -5 && deno test -A tests/usage-authority.test.ts 2>&1 | tail -5`
- History:
  - 2026-08-25 17:10 UTC — **AUTHOR SELF-REVIEW, not the independent review the lifecycle requires.** The product owner asked for the review directly, so it was done by the same session that wrote the change. Recorded as such: a self-review cannot cover what the author was blind to, which is the whole point of the different-model rule. Four defects were found across the three changes and fixed in one commit; details in each entry below. An independent pass is still worth having on the durable key routing and thread-id validation.
  - 2026-08-25 17:10 UTC — self-review found two defects in this change. **HIGH:** the durable thread-id charset admitted `..`; `encodeURIComponent("..")` is `".."`, so the key reached a directory name and was refused only because OPFS happens to reject it. The original test covered `../escape` (already rejected for the slash) and not the bare form — the test looked thorough and was not. Dots removed from the charset; `..`, `.` and the length bound are now covered. **MEDIUM:** making the index persist meant every deleted thread leaked `durable/threads/<id>` forever, against the memory-resilience constraint; `deleteThread` now reclaims it best-effort. Both fixed in `6320fd8`.
  - 2026-08-25 16:05 UTC — **all three failures resolved; the suite is green.** The usage-authority probes were fixed independently by another lane (`ced852d`). The remaining two were one product bug and one stale test, not the same thing.
  - 2026-08-25 16:05 UTC — **P0 product bug.** `agent.run` returned `invalid durable-run key: thread-runs:<threadId>` for EVERY task. The 0.2.257 log redesign (`ee970b3`) added a `thread-runs:<threadId>` reverse index written through `durableRunMemory`, but the durable key router only understood `run-registry` and the five `run*:<executionId>` prefixes; a thread id is not an execution id, so `durableStoreForKey` threw, and because every run links its thread on the way in the throw took the run with it. The router now gives `thread-runs:` its own bounded per-thread store mirroring the per-execution layout, `keys()` enumerates them, and thread ids are validated against a bounded safe charset (`thread-runs:../escape` and an empty id are rejected). No migration: the feature never successfully wrote a key. This single bug was killing the five journey checks that ask the agent to actually produce a result.
  - 2026-08-25 16:05 UTC — **stale test, product correct.** The suite aborted at "pending owner approval did not render in exact Settings" and lost the last 30 checks. `ab02213` made `asset.delete`/`agent.delete`/`named-agent.delete`/`recipe.delete` owner-direct, so an owner surface click no longer queues an approval; three journey steps still waited for a row that is now correctly never created. Disenroll now asserts the new behaviour POSITIVELY (a genuine owner click leaves no `agent.delete` approval queued) rather than simply dropping the old assertion, and the deny/worker-restart paths moved to `asset.update`, which is still gated and exercises the identical deny flow — coverage preserved, not removed.
  - 2026-08-25 14:40 UTC — opened with attribution evidence. **Chrome journeys: 96/126**, aborting at `journey failure: pending owner approval did not render in exact Settings`, immediately after `Settings: Disenroll button present for an enrolled agent`; the remaining 30 checks report `(not reached)`. **Unit: `tests/usage-authority.test.ts` PROBE-2** ("a concurrent initializer loser must mirror the WINNING authority, not its own" — `authority holds the migrated legacy row exactly once`) **and PROBE-4** ("after corruption repair, a valid write succeeds") fail. All three were reproduced on pristine `0626e6b` with unrelated local work stashed, and again with it restored, at the identical abort point — so they predate that work and are not caused by it. Filed rather than fixed in passing: the journey abort sits in the approvals/enrollment path and the usage probes in the ledger, both owned by other lanes.

  severity: P2

  severity: P3
  status: merged
