- id: CAP-FB-20260826-PERMISSIONS-SIMPLIFY-01
  severity: P0
  status: merged
  summary: "Owner (frustrated, P0): the permission system is a MESS. (1) The sorting-hat demo failed with 'Tab grouping write operations are pending owner tab-management permission enrollment in Settings' EVEN THOUGH all permissions are enabled — there are TWO confusing layers (the chrome API permission AND the separate expiring browser-control GRANT) and the owner can't tell which one to grant. (2) 'It should be asking me in context' — when a tool needs a permission/grant, the approval must surface IN the agent/task context, not send the owner to a Settings page. (3) Settings UI can't REMOVE a permission; the 'needs permission' security label never surfaces where to manage it. GOAL (owner's words): 'make it super simple and easy to use and understand.' REDESIGN: (a) ONE coherent mental model — when a tool needs something, an approval surfaces in-context ('This agent wants to group tabs — Allow?') and one click grants what's needed; (b) diagnose why the demo said 'pending enrollment' despite enabled permissions (which layer failed — is the grant expiring/not-set, is tabGroups separate from tabs and un-granted, or a real detection bug?); (c) Settings becomes a clear inventory — every permission with a plain-English label + what it enables + a working add/remove toggle, and 'needs permission' labels link to the exact control; (d) the in-context approval is the primary path, Settings is the management/inventory path. ACCEPTANCE: the sorting-hat demo works after a single in-context approval; every permission is add/removable in Settings with a plain-English label; no 'pending enrollment' dead-ends. LANDED 0.2.303 (0856225f) + 0.2.313 (5f8931f3) — in-context approval cards for tool permission/grant denials; one click grants exactly the needed scope and retries; deny is sticky; the Settings dead-end is gone. The tabGroups half of the sorting-hat failure was a genuinely undeclared permission, fixed at 0.2.290."
- id: CAP-FB-20260826-BROWSER-SINGLE-DRIVER-01
  severity: P1
  status: merged
  summary: "Owner requirement (2026-08-26): with many NTPs/surfaces open, ONLY ONE may issue browser commands at a time. Today the grantMutex serializes the grant-check+mutation per-tool in the SW realm, but nothing arbitrates WHICH surface drives — multiple NTPs can interleave destructive commands from different agents. DESIGN: a SW-owned, durable, expiring BROWSER-CONTROL SESSION LEASE — a single holder keyed by surface/run; a surface must hold the lease to issue destructive browser commands; a competing surface gets an honest 'another surface is driving the browser' result (or a bounded queue); released on task end / surface close / expiry. In the worker architecture the lease authority stays in the SW and each agent worker requests the lease before driving the browser (recorded in docs/AGENT-EXECUTION-ARCHITECTURE.md). ACCEPTANCE: two NTPs drive concurrently → exactly one succeeds, the other is honestly told why; the lease survives the issuing surface closing (expiry-based release); no deadlock on lease release. LANDED 0.2.310 (a7612031, b8896f0d, 95521139) — a SW-owned, durable, expiring single-driver lease. Both the worker and the interactive paths go through withGrantLock; the check is DESTRUCTIVE-only so capture_screenshot stays an ungated read."
- id: CAP-FB-20260826-AGENT-WORKERS-01
  severity: P0
  status: merged
  summary: "Owner DECISION (2026-08-26): adopt the per-agent SHARED WORKER execution architecture (docs/AGENT-EXECUTION-ARCHITECTURE.md). Each agent (background/named/site) = its own shared worker ({name: agentId}), hosted by the single offscreen document (reason WORKERS — the SW cannot create workers directly), bootstrapped through the SW (alarms wake SW → SW ensures offscreen host + worker alive → dispatch). MessagePorts passed to CLIENTS (NTP/sidepanel) via a SW-validated handshake so the UI holds a live port and keeps the worker alive 'as much as possible'. BroadcastChannel (cap:agent:<id>) for state. SW stays the authority for routing/auth/grant-lock/redaction/storage. PHASES: P1 foundation (offscreen host bootstrap + agent-worker shared-worker shell + SW connect/port handshake + alive-set reconciliation + documented pattern) → P2 migrate the agent-do run loop into the worker (tool exec, provider calls, durable-run interaction from the worker context) → P3 durability mapping (run progress/logs survive worker death via durable-runs/OPFS) → P4 UI ports everywhere + background agents fully on workers. Acceptance per phase; P1 KATs: bootstrap, port handshake, keep-alive across host/client death, reconcile-on-wake. LANDED — all four phases: P1 0.2.308 (d0060d28), P2 0.2.309 (e7bf6b81, 90d32754), P3 (1e0588c4), P4 0.2.310 (a7612031). Each agent runs in its own shared worker with authority staying in the SW."

title: [CAP-FB-20260827-MAIN-GATES-RED-02] Main is red again: the journey suite drives a deleted Settings section
description:
## [CAP-FB-20260827-MAIN-GATES-RED-02] Main is red again: the journey suite drives a deleted Settings section
- Feedback: 2026-08-27 — found by running the gates during a documentation reconciliation, not by reading trackers. `npm run test:chrome` reports **26/127** on clean `origin/main@139b6f92` (`0.2.319`) with no local changes
- Updated: 2026-08-27 22:40 UTC
- Status: DONE
- Priority: P0
- Owner: claude-opus-5 implementer session
- Workspace: active (local path private)
- Branch: working tree on `origin/main`
- Base: `139b6f92`
- Candidate: `9f02f9fc` (0.2.320)
- Shipping: `origin/main@9f02f9fc` (0.2.320, pushed 2026-08-28)
- Acceptance: `npm run test:chrome` reaches 127/127 (or an honestly re-baselined count) on a clean profile. Each of the three failures is resolved at the layer that actually broke — the deleted-section drive is repointed at the in-context approval path so the deny/restart coverage it carried is **preserved, not deleted**; the capability-count assertion is derived from `CAPABILITIES` rather than hard-coded; and the `debugger` assertion is left failing until Q17 is decided, then made to match the decision. No assertion is weakened to make the suite pass
- Review: **author review 2026-08-27 with the falsification gates** (the review rule changed the same day — no second model is available; see AGENTS.md "Review without a second model"). The gates caught a real defect in my own change: see the History entry below
- Gates: Chrome journeys **127/127** · unit **1779/0** · security suite **PASS** · build clean · changelog in sync · gallery drift clean · tasks schema clean
- Blockers: —
- Next: closed. The remaining follow-up is generic — keep applying the falsification gate to every future assertion change
- Recover: `npm run test:chrome 2>&1 | grep -E "^FAIL|journey failure" | head`
- History:
  - 2026-08-28 00:30 UTC — **the falsification gate immediately caught a defect in my own fix, which is the whole argument for it.** Under the new rule every changed assertion must be shown going RED against the unfixed product. Two were checked. **(a) The debugger removal guard passed:** re-adding `"debugger"` to the manifest turned `T12 GUARD` red (13 passed / 1 failed), restoring it turned it green — so the guard genuinely protects the ten deleted tests. **(b) The capability assertion FAILED its falsification and had to be rewritten.** I had replaced the rotted literal `length === 7` with `capState0.length === CAPABILITIES.length`. Adding a phantom capability to `CAPABILITIES` and re-running left the journey at **127/127** — the check still passed. It was tautological: Settings renders its rows straight from `CAPABILITIES`, so both sides of the comparison move together and the count half can never fail. My "fix" was weaker than the hard-coded literal it replaced, and a plain reading of the diff would not have shown that. Rewritten to assert what is actually falsifiable — that the extension boots with zero capabilities granted, and that every capability this suite goes on to DRIVE is present by id. Falsified properly: renaming `sidePanel` to `sidePanelRENAMED` takes the suite to **125/127** with that exact check FAIL; restoring returns **127/127**.
  - 2026-08-27 21:15 UTC — opened with reproduction on clean main. **(1) The abort, and the reason the number is 26.** `scripts/chrome-journeys.ts:749` `resolveNextApproval` clicks `.nav-item[data-section="approvals"]` and throws `pending owner approval did not render in exact Settings`. `0.2.313` (`5f8931f3`) deliberately deleted that Settings section — approvals moved in-context, which was the right product change — but the journey was never repointed, so the throw takes the remaining 100 checks with it. The suite is reporting far worse than the product is, and that gap is itself the danger: a red number nobody trusts is a gate nobody reads. **(2) `manifest: debugger absent everywhere` fails honestly.** `0.2.286` (`38641974`) re-declared `"debugger"` in `optional_permissions` for the allowlisted CDP tools, reversing its deliberate removal at `c5ccb2d0`. The assertion is correct and the posture changed under it; this is an owner decision (Q17), not a test defect. **(3) `permissions: all seven capabilities start ungranted` fails.** `extension/lib/capabilities.js` now defines **18** capabilities, up from 7 across the `0.2.278`–`0.2.290` tool waves; the assertion hard-codes `length === 7`.
  - 2026-08-27 22:40 UTC — **all three fixed; the full suite is green (127/127, 1779/0, security PASS).** Deliberately NOT by relaxing assertions: **(1)** the approvals drive was repointed onto the product's real contract. `management.resolve-approval` is still gated on `context.principal === "owner-options"`, so resolving still demands the Settings surface; the Settings control now completes in ONE click through its native `confirmActionDialog`, driven with a genuine CDP click, matching what `runOwnerApprovedMutation` actually does. The two DOM-scraping approval assertions moved onto the **payload**, which is strictly stronger than scraping one rendering of it — the row must be singular, expose exactly `action,approvalId,at,targetRef`, carry a 32-char opaque `targetRef`, and leak no asset id, digest or raw target. The embedded-iframe deny check now evaluates inside the Settings frame's OWN execution context, because calling another frame's `chrome.runtime` from the parent realm does not adopt that frame's principal — so it now genuinely proves the embedded Settings surface is an owner principal, which the old version did not. **(2)** `debugger` removed per the owner decision (Q17): the optional permission, the four CDP tools, the capability row, the Settings label. Browser tools 130 → 126, capability table 159 → 155; the user-scripts half of T12 is untouched. A removal guard was ADDED (`tests/chrome-tools-t12.test.ts`) asserting absence from the manifest, the toolset, the scoped toolset, `BROWSER_TOOL_NAMES`, the capability table and the Settings capability list — deleting 10 tests without leaving a guard would have been the quiet way to lose this. **(3)** the capability count now reads `CAPABILITIES.length` from the product's own table instead of the literal `7`, so the next tool tranche cannot rot it.
  - 2026-08-27 21:15 UTC — **process finding, recorded because the defect is the symptom.** This is the second instance of the identical class: `CAP-FB-20260825-MAIN-GATES-RED-01` was opened on 08-25 for a journey suite left behind by a shipped change, fixed, and the same thing happened again within two days. The full-suite-green rule in `AGENTS.md` is not being applied at the moment work lands. Consequence: **no task merged since 2026-08-25 can legitimately be `DONE`**, since `DONE` requires the journey suite green at that tip — several entries claim it against a gate that was not actually green.

title: [CAP-FB-20260823-ARTIFACT-DELETE-PERMISSION-01] Artifact deletion should not require a hidden permission
description:
## [CAP-FB-20260823-ARTIFACT-DELETE-PERMISSION-01] Artifact deletion should not require a hidden permission

- Feedback: 2026-08-23 — product owner: deleting an artifact while viewing
  artifacts in the UI demands a permission, which it should not; worse, there
  is no way to know a permission is required because it is hidden in Settings
  and never re-surfaced after granting
- Updated: 2026-08-23 20:08 UTC
- Status: MERGED
- Resume: —
- Priority: P0
- Owner: unassigned
- Workspace: `/home/paulkinlan/worktrees/cap-artifact-delete-6a6c3a1`
- Branch: detached
- Base: `6a6c3a1eb538ded942d1c44949c261c4579d40e7`
- Candidate: GLM implementation (owner-direct `asset.delete` + native dialog + gates rows)
- Shipping: `origin/main@ab02213ffad0692fe484abd18eff266946440cad` (0.2.194)
- Acceptance: deleting an artifact from the artifact view succeeds as a direct
  owner action without any permission grant; if any capability genuinely
  requires a grant, the need is surfaced at the moment of the action as a
  native `<dialog>` modal explaining exactly what and why, and the same
  pattern applies everywhere a permission may be needed; Settings permission
  rows state which actions they gate; granting once never leaves a silently
  required but invisible dependency
- Review: pending independent permission-model, owner-authority, UX truth,
  accessibility, and loaded-MV3 review
- Gates: delete-from-view journey with and without any related grant; modal
  contents/name the capability and the action; deny/cancel mutate nothing;
  Settings row traceability; AX/keyboard/narrow/RTL/theme checks
- Blockers: must compose with `CAP-FB-20260819-PERMISSION-REMEDIATION-UX-01`
  (owner-only prompts and paused-run resume) and the artifact transaction
  authority; must not widen any host/site access grant
- Next: audit every artifact-delete path for permission dependencies and map
  which are real capability gates versus accidental orchestration artifacts
- Recover: `git grep -n "artifact.delete\|deleteArtifact\|permissions.request" -- extension`
- History:
  - 2026-08-25 — triage flip: landed earlier; verified on main.
  - 2026-08-23 20:08 UTC — captured from direct product-owner feedback as P0.
  - 2026-08-23 20:35 UTC — audit result: the ONLY artifact-delete surfaces are
    the artifacts gallery (owner UI), the model `delete_asset` management tool,
    and Settings approval resolution; NO Chrome permission is involved anywhere
    (artifacts live in OPFS). The "permission" was the owner-approval
    orchestration gate applied unconditionally — a real gate for model-initiated
    deletes, an accidental hidden dependency for direct owner clicks.
    Implementation: `OWNER_DIRECT_ACTIONS`/`isOwnerDirectApproval` (pure,
    lib/owner-approval.js) lets a browser-attested `extension`/`owner-options`
    document's `asset.delete` through with an `owner-direct` audit event; model
    and page principals keep the full approval flow; the gallery's
    `window.confirm` became a native `<dialog>` naming the artifact (Cancel and
    Escape mutate nothing); every Settings permission row now states the actions
    it gates (`gates` field, rendered on the row; storage's row states the OPFS
    artifact exemption); the Approvals section copy now says agent-initiated
    operations pause there and direct owner actions never do. Focused gates:
    owner-approval-security, diagnostics, capability-gates (new),
    tools-management, sw-route-modularization, artifacts, artifact-tx — 83/83.

## [CAP-FB-20260829-MAIN-GATES-RED-03] Journey suite red on main after the install-granted permission change
- Feedback: 2026-08-29 — found by running the suite on `origin/main`
- Updated: 2026-08-29 UTC

- Workspace: main
- Branch: main
- Base: `2c84f2fa`
- Candidate: —
- Shipping: —
- Acceptance: `npm run test:chrome` green at the tip, with the permission checks asserting the CURRENT install-granted model rather than deleted
- Review: author review 2026-08-29 with the falsification gate cleared
- Gates: journeys 120/120; unit 2243/0; build, tracker schema, gallery, vocabulary green
- Blockers: —
- Next: —
- Recover: `git grep -n "install-granted, not optional" -- scripts/chrome-journeys.ts`
- History:
  - 2026-08-29 — **fixed: 78/127 → 120/120.** Two of the three causes were product bugs the suite had correctly caught, not test drift.
    **(1) Test drift.** The product moved to 36 permanent install-granted permissions plus `host_permissions: ["<all_urls>"]`; the suite still drove `.grant-perm` / `.revoke-perm` controls that no longer exist. The 11 permission checks were rewritten as 4 that describe the real model: the manifest's install-granted shape, every capability granted at install (read from the worker's authoritative map rather than a DOM scrape that carried no ids), the Settings panel being a read-only diagnostic with zero controls, and `capability.revoke` still requiring owner approval. The enrollment and screenshot checks flipped from asserting a headless denial to asserting the now-reachable success path; refusal is still covered by the wrong-origin, expired-grant and post-revoke probes. `audioCapture`/`videoCapture` report not-granted under headless, so the panel check deliberately asserts read-only-ness rather than universal grantedness — otherwise it would fail for an environment reason.
    **(2) Product bug — every site-agent delete failed.** `unregisterOriginScripts` treated a per-origin host permission that `contains()` still reports as a teardown failure. Under `<all_urls>` that permission is permanent and `permissions.remove` cannot touch it, so deletion always returned `"host permission still present after remove"` despite having removed the scripts and cleared memory. Per-origin host revocation is now recognised as NOT APPLICABLE in that model, and the delete/retry routes no longer gate success on it. Their fallback error also claimed `"OPFS clear failed"` when clearing had succeeded; it now says what actually happened.
    **(3) Product bug — a revoke that could never succeed destroyed state first.** Every `capability.revoke` branch does its dependent teardown before removing the permission (scripting tombstones every enrolled origin so a running bridge is rejected from that instant). That ordering is right when revocation is possible, but a required manifest permission can never be removed — Chrome answers `"You cannot remove required permissions."` — so the operation took the origins' authority with it on the way to a guaranteed failure. `isRequiredCapability()` now refuses in `capabilities.js` before any branch runs. The journey asserts the corrected property directly: **a refused revoke tombstones NOTHING.**
    **Falsification:** removing the guard restores the destructive path and drives "a refused revoke tombstones NOTHING" RED (117/120); restoring returns 120/120. The delete fix was verified by observing the exact error string disappear from the route response between runs.

## [CAP-FB-20260829-SILENT-PROVIDER-RUN-01] WITHDRAWN — the provider gate does report itself; the harness was reading the wrong DOM
- Feedback: 2026-08-29 — raised by this session, then withdrawn by this session on better evidence

- Priority: P0

- Candidate: —

- Review: n/a

- Next: nothing. The one genuine observation that came out of it is tracked separately as `CAP-FB-20260829-PROVIDER-SET-NO-BASEURL-01`
- Recover: `git log --oneline --all --grep=SILENT-PROVIDER-RUN-01`
- History:
  - 2026-08-29 — **WITHDRAWN. The claim was false and the fault was in my measurement, not the product.** I reported that a keyed provider without host access produced "no assistant message, no error, no status, no approval card". It produces a correct, styled error bubble with a remediation action. Re-measured reading the conversation through its shadow root: with a valid base URL the transcript says *"the configured provider's exact origin is not granted / grant the exact provider origin in Settings, then run this task again"* with a **Fix in Settings** control, and `runConversationTurn` sets `state: "waiting-for-permission"` before it. My probe sampled `document.body.innerText.slice(-260)` — the composer area — and counted `message-bubble` elements in the light DOM, so it could not see anything the conversation had rendered inside `<agent-conversation>`'s shadow root. It reported silence because it was looking somewhere silent. The harness has been fixed to read the bubbles themselves; a harness that can report "nothing happened" when something did is worse than no harness, which is the same class of defect as `CAP-FB-20260829-FIXED-DEBUG-PORTS-01`. **The "Fix in Settings" routing is also deliberate, not a shortfall:** `runConversationTurn` documents that calling `chrome.permissions.request` after the asynchronous provider lookup is rejected by Chrome as not being a user gesture, so Settings is the only surface that can genuinely request it. That is a considered design, and the AGENTS.md rule it appeared to violate is in fact satisfied — the failure names the exact origin and offers the remedy.

title: [CAP-FB-20260905-WEBMCP-SITE-RESET-ASK-FENCE-01] Site reset must invalidate pending first-use ASK cards even with no stored decisions
description:
# eo4d independent exact-object review — REVISE

Reviewer: Astra (independent session/model from implementation). Date: 2026-09-05.

- Reviewed candidate: `25acd4671075f9a2291e3a9f953d2717e59587df`
- Base: `35ad5264f1c8b3d7c261fb358a2dbf89d27e5741`
- Tree: `7ff5b2d1e2d952c8c3a600c13933ee89cbe3f043`
- Worktree: `/home/paulkinlan/worktrees/cap-webmcp-consent-eo4d`, branch `cap-webmcp-consent-eo4d`; clean before and after review probe.
- Landing authority remains coordinator `01a06e79`. This report does not authorize another SHA.

## Blocking finding R1 — P1: a site reset with only ASK tools leaves outstanding first-use cards authorized

Locations: `extension/lib/site-tool-consent.js:339–343`; `extension/background/service-worker.js:7782–7784,7799`.

Repro: enroll a site with a new tool; start its genuine first-use request and leave the Allow/Deny card pending; in Settings choose either site-wide **Reset decisions** or **Disable automatic use** while there are no stored matching decisions. The storage reset returns success without advancing the consent revision (`removed.length === 0`). The Settings route likewise computes no `affected` consent rows and skips `invalidateSiteToolWork`. Consequently the old card's exact ASK snapshot still matches, and a late Allow can save automatic-use authority and proceed after the reset.

This violates requirement 4 and the packet's explicit pending-card reset fence. Per-tool ASK reset correctly advances the revision even when no stored decision exists; the site-wide route does not.

Independent executable evidence (external probe, importing the candidate's real storage/tools modules with its in-memory OPFS fixture):

```sh
npm run test:file -- /home/paulkinlan/cap-evidence/astra/eo4d-25acd467-review/reset-fence-probe.test.ts --filter 'review:'
```

- `all` reset: RED — expected `site_tool_consent_changed`, stale Allow instead succeeds; revision stays 0.
- `automatic` reset: RED — same failure and revision remains 0.
- Exact-tool ASK reset positive control: GREEN — the stale Allow is rejected.
- Result: **1 passed, 2 failed**, runner exit 1. These are assertion failures, not setup/tooling errors.
- Probe: `reset-fence-probe.test.ts`; output: `reset-fence-probe.log` in this report directory.

Required fix: make an explicit successful site reset establish a persisted invalidation boundary even if the materialized decision set is empty, and invalidate pending/in-flight work independent of the number of changed decision rows. Preserve sticky Deny for `automatic` mode. Add regression tests that observe these two stale-card cases fail before the fix and pass afterward, plus a loaded owner-action test showing the old card cannot dispatch/save consent after reset and a fresh use must ask again.

## Evidence checked and limitations

- Read-only diff/source review covered consent identity/revisions, sticky Deny, owner routes/resolver identity, audit store and production dispatch/publication seams, lazy authority, reset barriers, Settings/components, owner-local activity hydration, and associated tests.
- Exact candidate packet and current clean Git object verified. All **16** manifest-listed screenshot hashes and sizes match the supplied files.
- Personally inspected exact-candidate saved first-use/result and Settings light/dark/forced-colors/narrow/audit/final screenshots. The presentation and direct activity slice show substantial improvement over the historical r3 packet; this does not clear R1.
- Supplied logs checked: changed/full suite 3663/0; production build PASS; Chrome 369/370 with sole owned `dptw` expected-red; loaded WebMCP 137/0. These are implementer-run gates, not independent reruns here.
- Loaded acceptance manifest truthfully remains **OPEN / automated-variant**: the deep invocation branch uses pregranted permissions; fresh-profile picker/JIT uses shipped manifest. No claim of fully shipped-byte native-permission coverage.
- No Chrome launched under coordinator freeze. No source edits, commits, resets, amendments, or pushes performed in the candidate worktree.
- No second speculative concern is promoted to a finding. R1 alone requires REVISE.

## Disposition

**REVISE `25acd4671075f9a2291e3a9f953d2717e59587df`.** Preserve the immutable candidate; implement the correction in a new commit, refresh the relevant evidence, and request exact-object re-review through the coordinator.

Real storage regressions are RED on 25acd467 and GREEN on the fix. A loaded Settings reset while the first-use card is pending prevents the old card saving Allow or dispatching; fresh use asks again. Independent exact-object review and complete serial landing gates required.

title: S4 call path: execute_tool runs an uploaded module from an agent run and returns its stdout
description:
Fourth stage of chrome-agent-platform-9ux7, and the stage that carries the epic. Today the WASI executor is reachable ONLY from the owner-only Settings preview (service-worker.js 'wasm.preview.run' + previewSpecFor's trusted spec map, executed in the options document). This stage gives it a route reachable from an agent run.

WHAT: dispatching a 'user-wasm-task' tool call fetches the module bytes from the S1 store by digest, builds the WASI job from the call arguments (stdin text + argv), runs it through the EXISTING extension/lib/wasm-executor.js (fresh Worker per call, no main-thread fallback, wall deadline) and returns stdout as the tool result. Reuse the executor and the offscreen/options host — do not write a second execution path; if the existing host cannot be reached from a background run, extend it rather than fork it, and say in the bead comments which one you extended.

NO ADMISSION BOUNDS: no size, imports or memory gate before the call. The wall deadline STAYS and is not an admission bound — it is what lets a runaway module be terminated and reported honestly rather than hanging the run forever. A module that traps, refuses to instantiate, or exceeds the deadline produces an honest tool error the model can read and retry against, never a silent empty result.

APPROVAL: an uploaded module runs under the normal tool-approval flow, unchanged. That is the standing consent model for tools, not a new bound introduced here.

ACCEPTANCE (the epic's end-to-end proof): in a real loaded extension, upload a genuinely user-supplied .wasm (NOT one of the bundled CAS modules — the point is a module no gate ever approved), ask an agent to use it, and see the model call it and the module's real stdout come back in the transcript. Screenshot the run. Also prove the failure shape: a module that traps returns a readable error and the run continues.

FILES: extension/background/service-worker.js (dispatch), extension/lib/wasm-offscreen-host.js or the options host (route), tests/, scripts/kat-user-wasm-*.ts (new browser proof).
DEPENDS ON: S1, S3.

title: S3 catalog registration: an uploaded module appears as a real tool the agent can find
description:
Third stage of chrome-agent-platform-9ux7. Uploaded modules become live tool-catalog descriptors so search_tools can return them.

WHAT: a new sourceKind 'user-wasm' in extension/lib/tool-catalog.js (TOOL_SOURCE_KINDS) with an adapter beside adaptBundledTools, mapping S1 store rows to canonical descriptors: name = the owner's name, description = the owner's description (the model reads this), packageDigest = the sha256, dispatcherKind 'user-wasm-task', availability 'ready'. Wire it into buildToolCatalog's inputs in the service worker so the descriptors reach search_tools and the lazy tool protocol.

WHY A NEW SOURCE KIND rather than reusing 'bundled-package': provenance differs and the UI must be able to say so. A bundled module is pinned, licensed and SBOM'd in-repo; an uploaded one is the owner's own file. Same execution path, different origin story — and the catalog is where that distinction has to be legible.

The input schema is the WASI shape the executor already speaks: stdin text plus argv. Do not invent a per-module JSON schema in this stage — a module cannot declare one yet, and guessing produces a schema the model will trust and the module will ignore.

ACCEPTANCE: with one module uploaded, search_tools returns it with the owner's name and description; its descriptor carries the digest; removing the module removes it from the catalog within the same session (no reload). Falsification: drop the adapter from buildToolCatalog, watch the search test go red, restore.

FILES: extension/lib/tool-catalog.js, extension/background/service-worker.js, tests/tool-catalog*.test.ts.
DEPENDS ON: S1.
OUT OF SCOPE: actually running it (S4).

title: [CAP-FB-20260905-USER-WASM-UI-01] S2 add and remove uploaded WebAssembly files in Settings
description:
Second stage of chrome-agent-platform-9ux7. The owner-facing surface over the S1 store.

WHAT: a Settings section (Tool library is the natural home) that lets the owner pick a .wasm file, give it a NAME and a DESCRIPTION, and see what is installed with a Remove control per row. The description field must say plainly that this text is what the agent reads to decide when to call the tool — that is the single most important field on the form and users will not guess it.

NO ADMISSION BOUNDS: the picker accepts any .wasm the owner chooses. No size warning that blocks, no imports preview that refuses. If something about the module is worth SHOWING (its size, the imports it declares), show it as information, never as a gate.

DESIGN: every piece of UI is a reusable Web Component in extension/shared/components.js and appears in docs/components.html (check:gallery fails on drift). No emoji icons — inline SVG, currentColor. Untrusted text (the filename, anything read out of the module) renders with textContent, never innerHTML.

ACCEPTANCE: in a real loaded extension, pick a real .wasm, name it, describe it, see it listed; reload Settings and it is still listed; Remove takes it away and it stays gone after reload. Assert the CONTENT of the list (rows, the name the owner typed), never merely that a panel is visible — that blind spot is chrome-agent-platform-rfca and it is exactly how a P0 shipped green.

FILES: extension/options/options.html + options.js, extension/shared/components.js, docs/components.html, scripts/kat-* for the browser proof.
DEPENDS ON: S1 (the store).
OUT OF SCOPE: making the tool callable (S3/S4).

title: [CAP-FB-20260905-USER-WASM-STORE-01] S1 user-wasm store: digest-keyed unbounded OPFS with owner metadata
description:
First stage of chrome-agent-platform-9ux7. A pure-ish module plus its OPFS backing that holds user-supplied Wasm modules; no UI, no catalog, no execution.

WHAT: extension/lib/user-wasm-store.js — put(bytes, {name, description}), list(), get(digest), remove(digest). The key is the sha256 of the bytes (same identity scheme the bundled CAS uses, so digests are comparable across both tranches). Metadata: owner-written name, owner-written description (this is the text the MODEL sees, so it is product copy, not a filename), byte size, added-at, and the digest.

NO ADMISSION BOUNDS (owner decision on the epic): no size cap, no imports inspection, no memory tier, no refusal on a module that fails to parse — a module that will not instantiate is a call-time failure with an honest error, not an upload-time rejection. Storage failures (OPFS quota) surface the browser's own honest error; never a silent truncation and never a cap invented here.

WHY OPFS rather than chrome.storage: modules are megabytes; chrome.storage.local is the wrong shape and the repo already has OPFS helpers (extension/lib/opfs-tool-workspace.js) to follow for directory handling and error language.

ACCEPTANCE: round-trip a multi-megabyte module through put/get and get identical bytes back; two puts of the SAME bytes with different names do not duplicate the stored bytes (one CAS entry, and the second put is honest about which name won); list() returns metadata without reading the bytes; remove() deletes both the entry and its bytes. Falsification: break the digest computation, watch the round-trip test go red, restore.

FILES: extension/lib/user-wasm-store.js (new), tests/user-wasm-store.test.ts (new).
OUT OF SCOPE: the upload UI (S2), catalog registration (S3), execution (S4).

title: [CAP-FB-20260905-USER-WASM-UPLOAD-01] User-uploaded WebAssembly tools: upload + call path
description:
EPIC. Paul (2026-09-05): users upload their OWN .wasm modules and they become callable tools, like the bundled ones. Owner decisions ON RECORD for this epic: NO BOUNDED ADMISSION (no size cap, no imports allowlist gate, no memory-tier gate, no admission refusal) and NO WEB STORE (the extension is not store-hosted, so store-policy/remote-code compliance does not constrain this path). Where a bound is load-bearing for correctness rather than policy — a wall-clock deadline that lets a runaway module be terminated — keep it and say so honestly; never reintroduce an admission gate under another name.

WHERE THE CODE STANDS (read before implementing): there IS a real WASI execution path — extension/lib/wasm-executor.js (fresh Worker per call, no main-thread fallback, wall deadline, one-way transport), extension/lib/wasm-execution-worker.js, extension/lib/wasm-sync-workspace.js, extension/lib/wasm-offscreen-host.js. It is reachable ONLY from the owner-only Settings preview route: service-worker.js 'wasm.preview.run' resolves toolId through a TRUSTED SPEC MAP (previewSpecFor), fetches a pinned bundled manifest + CAS bytes from extension/wasm/, and executes in the options document. extension/lib/bundled-tool-packages.js ships every descriptor admitted:false/disabled:true with disabledReason 'no-execution-host' and states outright that nothing there registers a tool in the live catalog. tool-catalog.js already reserves sourceKind 'bundled-package' and dispatcherKind 'bundled-wasm-task' (adaptBundledTools), unused live.

So this epic is what makes Wasm tools LIVE — for user-supplied modules — and it necessarily builds the piece the bundled tranche is also waiting on: a real execution route reachable from an agent run rather than from Settings only.

ACCEPTANCE FOR THE EPIC: a user picks a .wasm file in Settings, gives it a name and a description, and an agent run can then find it via search_tools and call it via execute_tool, with its stdout coming back as the tool result — proven end to end in a real loaded extension with a genuinely user-supplied module (not a bundled one), at a size and with imports that no admission gate would have had to approve.

A loaded extension promotes/chains the exact 100 MiB input and 139,810,137-byte base64 output and verifies complete SHA-256/byte counts without exposing or duplicating the payload in extension messaging. title: Build search/grep/sed/awk/sort/uniq/wc/tr/base64/jq as real tools with NO size caps — investigate algorithms if performance is a concern, don't cap
description:
Owner directive 2026-09-04: Build the Unix/system tool family (grep, sed, awk, sort, uniq, wc, tr, base64, jq) as REAL tools with NO size caps. If there's a performance concern, investigate better algorithms (streaming, chunked processing, incremental parsing) — do NOT impose size limits. The dptw no-limits sweep already removed the self-imposed caps from existing tools; this bead extends that to the full Unix/system tool family admissions (chrome-agent-platform-ims).

DESIGN:
- Each tool reads/writes via streaming where possible (Read-able streams for input, incremental output for grep/sed)
- jq and awk need parsers — use a bounded grammar parser (not regex), which is O(n) and handles any size
- grep: streaming line-by-line match (O(n) regardless of file size)
- sort: external merge sort for datasets exceeding memory (investigate)
- No 'maxBytes', no 'maxLines', no content ceiling

ACCEPTANCE: each tool tested with a 100MB input; no size-related errors; correct output; performance measured and reported.

title: Pyodide WASM runtime: build, admit into CAS, and wire the load path so python_execute actually executes code
description:
The brv lane wired the python_execute tool definition, route, and capability gate — but the actual Pyodide WASM runtime was never built or admitted. When an agent calls python_execute, it correctly fails with 'the bounded Python runtime is not admitted yet' and falls back to showing the code as text. The owner wants actual execution.

WORK:
1. Download/build the Pyodide WASM distribution (pyodide.wasm + Python stdlib) — sized for the bounded CAS inventory
2. Admit the Pyodide artifacts into the bounded CAS inventory (exact CAS hashes, manifest with imports/exports)
3. Wire the load path: python-tool.js loads the Pyodide runtime lazily on first python_execute call
4. The runtime runs in the script-sandbox (no DOM, no network by default — fetch is host-listed)
5. Stdout/stderr capture and return to the agent
6. Falsification: print('Hello, World') returns 'Hello, World' (not a text description of the code)

ACCEPTANCE: python_execute({'code': 'print(1+1)'}) returns {'result': '2'} — actual execution, not a text fallback.

title: Show thinking tokens in the conversation when the provider streams them — collapsible trace under the thinking indicator
description:
Owner feature request 2026-09-03: when an agent is thinking, the user wants to see the actual thinking tokens streaming from the provider (available from Gemini, Claude, DeepSeek, and other models that expose chain-of-thought). Currently these tokens are either hidden or discarded. The user wants a collapsible dropdown under the 'thinking...' indicator that shows the thinking trace in real time as tokens arrive.

DESIGN:
- The conversation's run-status surface (the existing 'thinking...' indicator) gains a expandable section when thinking tokens are available from the provider
- Tokens stream in real time (same streaming mechanism as the response text)
- The section is collapsed by default; the user clicks to expand and see the live trace
- When thinking finishes, the section collapses and the response begins
- If the provider doesn't send thinking tokens, the section doesn't appear at all

IMPLEMENTATION:
1. The provider layer (models/*.js) already receives thinking tokens in the stream (reasoning_content, thinking blocks, etc.) — currently these are discarded or logged. Capture them and emit them as a new event type (e.g. 'thinking-token') through the existing streaming pipeline.
2. The conversation component (shared/conversation.js) receives the thinking stream and renders it in a collapsible section under the thinking indicator.
3. The collapsible section: collapsed by default, click-to-expand, live-streaming text inside, auto-scroll to bottom while expanded.
4. Provider-specific handling: Gemini (thought parts), Claude (thinking blocks), DeepSeek (reasoning_content field), OpenAI (if available).
5. The thinking trace is NOT persisted in the thread after the run completes — it's a live-streaming view only (unless the owner wants it saved, which is a follow-up).

ACCEPTANCE: a Gemini/Claude task with extended thinking shows the thinking trace streaming in the collapsible section; a task without thinking tokens shows no section; the trace is live (tokens appear as they arrive, not all at once); the section collapses when thinking ends; falsification-gated.
close_reason: MERGED @ 502fbd47 — live thinking trace: mounts on first reasoning token, collapsed-default with live count, streams, expands, auto-collapses at answer start, dropped at settle; KAT 10/10 twice on the exact object + falsification (case removed -> 7 RED). Supersedes the diverged 2e8777b8 (never landed, older gates).

title: Settings tool library shows 0 site tools (declared/inferred) — the shadow catalog reads hub scope and never includes per-origin WebMCP tools
description:
Owner report 2026-09-03: 'Site tools (declared)' in Settings shows 0 when browsing sites that have declared WebMCP endpoints (e.g. beads.gascity.com declares search_docs and open_skill). The content script discovers and reports them (tools-reported log confirms), but the Settings tool library never shows them.

ROOT CAUSE: readShadowCatalogInputs() (service-worker.js:3592) builds the shadow catalog from HUB-scope sources only: builtin tools, browser tools, management tools, and bundled packages. The per-origin WebMCP declared/inferred tools — which live in per-origin site toolsets built by siteToolset(origin, runGenCell) — are NEVER included because they exist only in per-origin contexts, not at the hub scope.

FIX: aggregate WebMCP declared/inferred tools across ALL enrolled origins and include them in the shadow catalog inputs under the 'webmcp-declared' and 'webmcp-inferred' source kinds. Each row should show the origin it belongs to (e.g. 'search_docs — beads.gascity.com') so the owner can see which sites have declared tools. The catalog already has the source kinds ('webmcp-declared', 'webmcp-inferred') in TOOL_SOURCE_KINDS — the data just never reaches it.

ACCEPTANCE: browse a site with declared WebMCP tools → Settings tool library shows them under 'Site tools (declared)' with the origin; browse a site with inferred tools → shows under 'Site tools (inferred)'; multiple origins' tools are aggregated; no tools → count is 0 (honest).
close_reason: Fixed on origin/cap-tool-library-sitetools-lmk2 @ b55f0380 (v0.3.66). TRUE root cause (different from the bead's description): the shadow catalog's origin loop existed since 08-22, but dptw removed TOOL_CATALOG_BOUNDS.maxDescriptors on 09-03 and the loop kept computing it — undefined*2 = NaN, slice(0, NaN) = [], so EVERY origin's declared/inferred tools were silently dropped and Settings showed 0. Fixed: removed the dead bound arithmetic (dptw: no size caps), added origin labels to summary rows (descriptor.scope.origin, bounded 2048), UI renders the site per row. Gates: new harness 5/0 (byte-faithful loop mirror proved RED=undefined counts before, GREEN after), related suites 33/0 + 17/0, full suite 342 files GREEN, build RC=0. Browser-journey residual (beads.gascity.com live browse) noted — unit chain is proven end-to-end.

title: Provider server tools toggle resets on reload — the init code is in renderAgents() but the toggle lives in the providers section (broken by multi-section navigation)
description:
Owner bug report 2026-09-03: 'provider server tools' is not set on reload. The multi-section navigation change (0181699e) introduced ensureSectionRendered() which lazily mounts section renderers. The server-tools init code (state load + toggle listener + renderServerToolAgents) lives inside renderAgents() (line 1303) which is called by ensureSectionRendered('agents') — but the server-tools toggle HTML (#server-tools-enabled) is in the PROVIDERS section. On page reload, navigating to providers calls renderProviders() which doesn't touch server tools — the toggle stays unchecked even though the setting was persisted.

FIX: extract the server-tools init into its own function (initProviderServerTools) and call it from ensureSectionRendered('providers') alongside renderProviders(). Ensure renderAgents() no longer double-initializes it (guard with a flag or move the init entirely out of renderAgents()).

ACCEPTANCE: reload the page → navigate to Providers → the server tools toggle shows the persisted state; toggling saves and the state persists across reload; agents section still renders correctly.
close_reason: FIXED on origin/cap-beads-wuvg @ 3671fe66 (fix) + 03661a03 (browser KAT) + 5ac37890 (changelog). Root cause: server-tools init lived in renderAgents() but the toggle HTML is in the providers section; multi-section lazy mount meant reload → providers never initialized it. Fix: extracted initProviderServerTools(), called from ensureSectionRendered('providers') after renderProviders(); renderAgents no longer touches server tools; sub-panel visibility now also requires the developer flag (paid dev feature stays dev-gated) with a flip-on resync. title: Site-agent search_docs on beads.gascity.com still throws opaque 'DOMException: UnknownError' — and the agent needs a docs-fallback path when site tools fail
description:
Owner follow-up 2026-09-03 (after the ajcc fix landed @ 89f91ccb): invoking search_docs/open_skill on beads.gascity.com via @-mention STILL returns 'DOMException: UnknownError (an internal exception in the documentation site's client-side search/storage engine)' with no useful diagnostics. Two problems:

1. THE OPAQUE ERROR PERSISTS: ajcc fixed the redaction/classification layer, but the error the owner sees is still the raw DOMException from the PAGE-SIDE dispatcher — our extension is relaying the page's own error honestly, but the page's handler throws unhelpfully. Diagnose WHY the page-side handler throws: is it the site's localStorage/IndexedDB in a restricted context, a CORS/CSP issue on the beads.gascity.com side, the WebMCP dispatch layer unavailable in this Chromium, or our bridge mangling the call? Instrument the dispatch boundary (per ajcc's honest-errors work) and capture the actual page-side stack.

2. THE AGENT NEEDS A DOCS FALLBACK: when a site's declared tools fail, the agent should have a fallback — fetch the site's documentation directly (https://beads.gascity.com has a well-structured docs site: /core-concepts, /workflows, /getting-started/quickstart, /cli-reference) via the platform's fetch/read-page tools, and answer from that. The agent should TRY the site's tools first, and on failure FALL BACK to fetching the docs page — not just report failure.

3. THE REAL ROOT CAUSE: the site declares WebMCP tools (search_docs, open_skill) but Chrome's native WebMCP dispatch may be unavailable in this Chromium build (no document.modelContext even with flags — per ajcc's investigation). If that's confirmed, the error should say exactly that ('this site declares WebMCP tools but your browser does not currently expose the WebMCP dispatch layer — open the page directly or fetch its documentation instead').

ACCEPTANCE: (a) instrumented repro against beads.gascity.com capturing the real page-side error; (b) the honest error names the actual cause; (c) a fallback path: agent fetches https://beads.gascity.com docs pages and answers the owner's question even when search_docs fails; (d) falsification tests for the fallback trigger (search_docs fails → fetch fires) and the honest error content.
close_reason: Landed on main (f474819e verified ancestor): dispatch fall-through + docs fallback + watchdog; review PASS

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
Worker report (cap-beads-922q @ e6bb53fe, pushed; local==origin confirmed).

ROOT CAUSE: on native-WebMCP Chrome, document.modelContext.executeTool throws DOMException: UnknownError from Chrome's native dispatch layer while the page's own handler is healthy (proven: ajcc's realsite probe ran the real beads.gascity.com handler to completion under a shim). The declared-tool dispatcher tried executeTool FIRST and gave up on throw — the page's own execute fn was never tried. Reproduced exactly in a real browser via new fixture tools (dispatch_broken_*): pre-fix RED shows the owner's exact error text.

FIX (dispatch chain, main-world.js): executeTool → tool.execute/_execute (identity-preserved from getTools) → callTool/invoke; a throwing path falls through; only ALL-paths-failing reports, attaching the full tried-chain to the LAST failure's honest description (real name/message/stack preserved — ajcc invariants intact; single redaction pass: a second pass NFKC-folds the redaction marker, caught by KAT). Accepted tradeoff (documented in code): a path that ran the handler then threw can re-run it in the next path.

title: Task composer: steer (redirect/stop the running agent) and queue (enqueue follow-up messages like the pi framework)
description:
Owner feature request 2026-09-03: when a task is queued or the owner replies while an agent is RUNNING, the composer should offer the two interactions the pi framework does well:

1. STEER — reply to the RUNNING agent and redirect it live: the new message is injected into the in-flight run (the agent sees it as guidance and adjusts course). Optionally with force options: steer-gently (inject as context), steer-and-stop-current-step, or stop-the-run outright. The pi model: typing while running steers; nothing is lost.
2. QUEUE — enqueue follow-up messages that the agent processes AFTER the current turn/run completes (a real queue with visible pending items: '2 queued messages', reorderable/removable before they fire). Today a queued message either races the run or is lost.

REQUIREMENTS:
- The composer detects a running task and offers both affordances explicitly (Send-now-stop / Steer / Queue) with keyboard shortcuts.
- Steered messages appear in the transcript as owner interruptions with their own visual treatment; queued messages appear as pending chips above the composer.
- Steer plumbing exists at the run level (the agent-worker architecture has the message ports — extend the protocol with a steer control message the run loop honors between steps).
- Queue plumbing: per-thread FIFO drained at run end, persisted across reloads (the durable run journal already stores thread state — reuse it).
- Falsification tests: steer mid-tool-call changes the agent's next action (fixture agent asserts the steering message arrived between steps); queue-while-running fires messages in order after completion and survives reload; stop-the-run cancels cleanly (no orphaned durable run).
- Works for named agents, background agents, and site agents alike (one protocol, all surfaces).
notes: Landed on branch cap-beads-afiu @ a8a92b31 (not merged to main). Steer+queue implemented: lib/run-control.js control plane (live-run steer store + durable per-thread kv FIFO), between-step model-seam injection in lib/agent.js + lib/agent-loop.js (fixture-verified: steer mid-tool-call changes the agent's next action; stop-step ends the loop at the next step boundary; stop-run never injected as text), agent-worker:steer protocol route, run.control.* owner-gated SW routes, NTP composer Steer/Queue/Send-now bar + persisted reorderable/removable pending chips, steer bubbles rendered as owner interruptions, drain-one-item-per-settled-run queue firing. Gates: npm run build green; deno test tests/ = 3187 passed / 0 failed. Not yet browser-journey verified (that is the merge coordinator's gate).

title: Generated sandboxed UI artifacts use unavailable APIs (localStorage etc.) — the agent must KNOW the sandbox constraints, and runtime errors must teach rather than just throw
description:
Owner bug report 2026-09-03: generated interactive artifacts (games/UI) run in a srcdoc sandbox WITHOUT allow-same-origin, so localStorage, sessionStorage, and other storage/permission-gated APIs are UNAVAILABLE — the agent keeps generating code that uses them, and the artifacts break at runtime ('guarded fallbacks' throw on restricted permissions). The agent has no way to know, so it makes the same mistake every time.

WORK:
1. TELL THE AGENT UP FRONT: the create_asset/append tool schema + the generating system prompt gain an explicit constraint block: 'the artifact runs in an origin-opaque sandbox: no localStorage/sessionStorage/cookies; no cross-origin fetches without CORS; no permission-gated APIs. Persist state IN-MEMORY in the artifact, or ask the platform to store data for you.' Keep it bounded (schema description, not a prompt essay).
2. RUNTIME ERRORS THAT TEACH: the sandbox error path currently surfaces raw DOMExceptions ('SecurityError: The document is sandboxed...'). Wrap/guard the known-broken API surfaces so the thrown error says WHAT to do instead: 'localStorage is unavailable inside sandboxed artifacts — keep state in a variable, or store it with the platform's asset/memory tools.' The error text is the teaching moment at exactly the moment of failure.
3. BLOB/PLATFORM ALTERNATIVES (evaluate, don't guess): where persistence is genuinely needed, evaluate (a) in-memory + export/import affordances, (b) the platform's asset tools as the persistence layer (agent writes state snapshots via append/asset tools), (c) OPFS-in-sandbox viability. Recommend one with evidence in the bead; do not build all three.
4. EVAL HARNESS: extend the artifact generation evals with a case asserting the composed guidance reaches the model and a fixture generation avoids localStorage (falsification: guidance removed → the fixture generation using localStorage must be flagged by the eval's checker).
Related: chrome-agent-platform-dptw (no-limits sweep), chrome-agent-platform-ajcc (site-tool honest errors).
close_reason: Closed

comments.text:
IMPLEMENTED on origin/cap-beads-np64 @ 2cf8f5ec (pushed 2026-09-03). Three layers + eval:

(1) THE AGENT IS TOLD UP FRONT — constraint block added to BOTH carriers:
    - Tool schemas (extension/lib/management-tools.js): create_asset, generate_ui carry the full block ("origin-opaque sandbox: NO localStorage/sessionStorage/cookies, NO network, NO permission-gated APIs — keep state IN-MEMORY or store state with the platform (a saved-state artifact/memory key)"); update_asset + patch_asset repeat it for the edit path.
    - The generating system prompt: new PROTECTED runtime-policy rule id "sandboxed-artifacts" (lib/runtime-policy.js) — it composes into every scope's final prompt layer, so owner prompt overrides can never remove it. Prompt budget kept < 6144 B (composed hub now 6135) by trimming unpinned master-skill prose and tightening the policy header/footer wording; constraints layer version bumped 1.1.0 -> 1.2.0 in the registry.

(2) RUNTIME ERRORS TEACH — sandboxApiGuardScript (shared/components.js) is injected into every generated-document frame via injectFrameGuards (after CSP/navguard/bootstrap, before generated code). Verified-in-Chrome surfaces are wrapped so the throw names the fix instead of the raw SecurityError: localStorage/sessionStorage, document.cookie writes, indexedDB, caches, OPFS navigator.storage.getDirectory, fetch. localStorage throw is near-verbatim from the issue: "localStorage is unavailable inside sandboxed artifacts - keep state in a variable, or store it with the platform's asset/memory tools". The script-sandbox host (extension/sandbox/script-sandbox.js) got the same teaching guards for storage surfaces (fetch stays the controlled host-bridged api there).

(3) PERSISTENCE ALTERNATIVES — RECOMMENDATION: in-memory as the artifact's only local state + the platform's asset/memory tools as the durable layer (agent stores snapshots on the owner's request). Evidence (real headless-Chrome CDP probe of an allow-scripts opaque frame, saved at worktree evidence-np64/sandbox-api-probe.log + red/green logs): localStorage/sessionStorage read -> SecurityError sandboxed; document.cookie write -> SecurityError; indexedDB.open -> SecurityError "access ... denied in this context"; caches -> SecurityError; OPFS navigator.storage.getDirectory() -> "Storage directory access is denied because the context is sandboxed and lacks the 'allow-same-origin' flag"; storage.estimate -> "not supported in this context"; fetch under the frame CSP -> opaque "Failed to fetch". So (c) OPFS-in-sandbox is NOT viable (opaque origin has no origin-keyed storage at all — Chrome refuses every storage API). In-memory + platform-store is the only stack that works today; an export affordance is the artifact rendering its state as copyable text that the agent then saves. NOT building all three: only the in-memory + platform-store guidance shipped (in the rule/schemas/guard), OPFS explicitly rejected with probe evidence.

(4) EVAL HARNESS — tests/artifact-sandbox-guidance-eval.test.ts (6 scenarios): composed prompt carries the constraint (hub + worker); create_asset/generate_ui + update_asset/patch_asset schemas carry it; the eval's fixture checker flags a localStorage-using generation and passes an in-memory one (this case is GREEN even with the guidance removed — the checker judges the generation text, the issue's falsification); the guarded frame carries the teaching guard before generated code; the shipped guard BEHAVES against shims (localStorage access throws the teaching sentence, cookie writes throw, OPFS/fetch reject with teaching text).

r5 review P1 #3 — persistence recommendation, ONE with evidence: RECOMMEND (b) the platform's asset tools as the persistence layer, with (a) in-memory as the runtime default (the issue's export/import affordance is inherent: the artifact IS the stored document).

title: Site-agent tool calls to declared page tools (e.g. search_docs on beads.gascity.com) always fail: 'DOMException: UnknownError from the page-side dispatcher' — opaque, unloggable, unreproducible from the error alone
description:
Owner bug report 2026-09-03: a task calling a site agent invokes the site's declared tool (e.g. search_docs({query:'installation'}) on https://beads.gascity.com) and ALWAYS errors: Status Failed, 'DOMException: UnknownError from the page-side dispatcher — The site's search handler threw an internal DOM exception during execution.' No console errors, no logs that explain the cause. Owner suspects content-script realm isolation (main world vs isolated world) or the page-side dispatch plumbing.

WHAT'S WRONG BEYOND THE BUG ITSELF: the error is opaque by construction — 'UnknownError' with no underlying cause surfaced, no page-console capture, no dispatch trace. Even if the fix were trivial, the diagnosis path is broken.

WORK:
1. REPRODUCE with instrumentation: drive a site-agent task against beads.gascity.com's search_docs in a loaded extension with the page-side dispatcher instrumented (wrap the dispatch/handler invocation in try/catch that serializes the REAL error: name, message, stack, and the realm it came from). Capture what actually throws — candidates: structured-clone of non-cloneable results across the content-script ↔ page boundary; the handler running in the ISOLATED world while the site registered it in MAIN world (or vice versa); response serialization failing (functions/symbols/DOM nodes in the result); a missing content-script bridge for the specific message shape; CSP blocking a page-side eval path.
2. FIX the actual failure layer.
3. HONEST ERRORS as a deliverable: the tool-result error must carry the underlying cause (error name/message/stack excerpt from the page side), the realm where it occurred, and the target origin — 'UnknownError' alone is a defect. If the page's handler genuinely throws DOMException with no detail, say exactly that and include everything the boundary captured.
4. Falsification tests: a fixture page declaring a tool whose handler throws a specific DOMException — the agent-visible error must contain that specificity; a fixture whose handler returns a non-cloneable value — must surface the serialization failure honestly; the happy path round-trips.
Related: the WebMCP/site-tool dispatch seams (content-script bridge, page-side dispatcher).

title: Test suite runtime: massively optimise deno test (target selection, dependency-aware subsetting, parallelisation) — more tests must not mean proportionally slower gates
description:
Owner feedback 2026-09-02: the deno test command takes way too long (~5-10 min per full run and growing). Adding features adds tests (good), but the gate time grows linearly with them. Want options + implementation to massively optimise how tests run, and ways to TARGET tests:

Investigate and implement (evidence for each option: measured before/after on the full suite):
1. PARALLELISATION — does the suite run files in parallel? deno test runs test modules concurrently by default but per-file serialization/permissions/shares may serialize. Measure: --parallel flag behaviour, per-file timing histogram (top-10 slowest files), whether slow files dominate.
2. TARGETED RUNS — a dependency-aware subset picker: a script that maps changed files (git diff --name-only origin/main) -> the test files that import/exercise them (static import graph), running ONLY those + the always-on core (security, vocabulary). This becomes the per-commit gate; the full suite stays the pre-merge/land gate.
3. ACTIONABLE npm scripts — npm test:changed / npm test:file -- <path> / npm test:fast (core + changed) so agents and the owner can target without thinking.
4. SHARED FIXTURE COST — the suite spends large time in fake-indexeddb/extension-boot fixtures per file; consider a shared test server-mode (deno test --parallel + module-level singleton fixtures) or moving heavy integration journeys out of the unit gate entirely.
5. REPORT the histogram + the chosen architecture in the bead before implementing (a design comment), so the owner can steer.

ACCEPTANCE (falsification-gated): full-suite wall time reduced measurably (record before/after); test:changed runs in <60s on a typical one-file change and catches a known regression injected into a changed seam (RED/GREEN proof); no test weakened or skipped — subsetting must be additive tooling, the full suite remains the merge gate.
close_reason: Closed

title: read_file refuses files over a 2000-byte maxBytes bound (fs_file_too_large) — reading any file must work; LLM-transport is an attachment concern, not a refusal
description:
Owner bug report 2026-09-02: read_file on a file from a granted directory handle fails with 'The file is too large to read within the bounded limit' (code fs_file_too_large, maxBytes 2000, path cairn-gateway/README.md, size 9080). A 9KB README is refused because the default bound is 2,000 BYTES — an absurd placeholder.

OWNER DIRECTIVE: read_file must work with ANY file size. The tool reads from the file handle locally — size is irrelevant to the read itself. If the content must reach the LLM's context, the system works out HOW to deliver it: attach as a file reference the model can read in chunks (offset/limit reads), summarize, or pass through to another tool — never a flat refusal at a tiny bound.

FIX:
1. Find the maxBytes=2000 default in the fs tool family (grep fs_file_too_large / maxBytes in extension/lib/ + the fs tools seam) and remove the refusal path for reads backed by a real handle.
2. read_file returns the complete content; the run-transport layer decides delivery: below the model-context budget -> inline; above -> attach via the existing file-attachment/retained-payload mechanism (retainedPayloadRef) so the model can request chunks (support offset/length params on read_file for chunked reads of huge files).
3. If a genuine transport budget exists, the error becomes actionable guidance ('file is 9KB; use offset/limit or ask for a summary') rather than fs_file_too_large at 2000 bytes.
4. Falsification tests: a 9KB file reads completely (the exact owner repro); a 10MB file reads via offset/limit chunking; no read is refused on size alone when a handle exists.

Related: chrome-agent-platform-kmpq (remove the 256KiB storage truncation regime), chrome-agent-platform-p45y (artifact size truncation). This is the same no-silly-caps family: tools must not refuse real work at placeholder bounds.
close_reason: Closed

title: Generated interactive artifacts: click events don't reach the artifact, and generated code appears truncated at size bounds
description:
Owner bug report 2026-09-02 (Telegram, voice):

SYMPTOM A — interactivity: when an agent generates an interactive artifact (e.g. a little game), CLICK EVENTS don't get through in the artifact view. Owner suspects the double-iframe (artifact iframe nested inside the hub's view frame) or some layer above it swallowing pointer events. Investigate: (a) iframe nesting + any overlay from the view chrome (frame bar, [data-embedded] rules from the one-shell merge) capturing pointer events; (b) the artifact iframe's sandbox/allow attributes — do they permit scripts + pointer interaction; (c) z-index/stacking of .view-frame vs artifact canvas; (d) whether the wheel/click hit-testing added for the dialog scroll work (chrome-journeys probes) interacts. Repro: ask an agent to build a click-based game; open the artifact; click buttons. Falsification-gated journey: synthetic click lands on a button inside the artifact iframe and increments visible state.

SYMPTOM B — truncation: the generated code sometimes looks CUT OFF in the artifact source view, and generation itself may be truncated at a size bound (owner has seen artifacts 'cut at certain sizes'). Two suspects to verify and fix separately: (1) the artifact WRITE path caps content (write_file/artifact tool bounds — check the artifact-tx bounds and any 64KiB-class limits on tool args); (2) the SOURCE VIEW renders truncated text (source view reading the rendered DOM/text slice instead of the complete stored content — same family as the copy-reads-DOM bug). The generation model may also stop early if the tool-call args cap applies — check whether write_file tool-call arguments are byte-capped at the protocol layer (lazy-tool-protocol / agent-do) and whether that cap is honest to the model (the model should be told the cap BEFORE generating, or streaming/appending writes should be supported: write_file in chunks).

ACCEPTANCE: (A) a generated click-game is fully interactive in the artifact view (journey with a real synthetic click asserting state change, screenshot evidence); (B) an artifact larger than any legacy bound stores COMPLETE (size asserted end-to-end: what the model wrote == what the source view shows == what runs), the source view shows the COMPLETE stored content byte-for-byte, and if a protocol cap exists it is either removed (payloads by reference, see chrome-agent-platform-kmpq) or surfaced to the model with a chunked-append write path. Related: chrome-agent-platform-kmpq (storage truncation regime removal).

title: Remove the 256KiB memory-store truncation for agent responses and thread data — OPFS/journal becomes the complete store, no more silent-feeling caps
description:
Owner directive 2026-09-02 (high priority): the 240KiB/256KiB store and outbox bounds are wrong. 'I don't want limits. Agent responses, data that can be used in threads and a whole bunch of other stuff like the truncation — it's incredibly dumb. We need to get it fixed.' A recent bug: outbox records stall at the 256KiB memory-store limit.

REDESIGN: agent responses and thread payloads must be stored COMPLETE, without memory-store size caps dictating truncation.
- Primary storage for large payloads moves to OPFS / the durable run journal (the retainedPayloadRef mechanism ALREADY exists — threads.js comments say the complete text stays in the durable run journal via retainedPayloadRef). The memory-store row keeps only a bounded INDEX/summary + a reference to the complete payload.
- Threads must hydrate the COMPLETE response from the journal/OPFS on open (no truncation marker as the end-user experience; the marker/digest may remain only as a loading affordance, not a cap).
- The outbox serialized into memory stays small BY DESIGN (references, not payloads) — records no longer stall at 256KiB because payloads never live there.
- Remove/adjust the bounds constants (threads.js MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES 240KiB, MAX_THREAD_BYTES 248KiB) as PRODUCT bounds; they may remain only as per-ROW summaries, not content caps.
- Migration: existing truncated threads backfill from the journal where the complete text exists (retainedPayloadRef); where it does not, the marker stays honest about what is lost.

ACCEPTANCE (falsification-gated): a 10MiB agent response is fully persisted (journal/OPFS) and rendered COMPLETE when the thread is opened; the memory-store row for that thread stays under the 256KiB store bound (index+ref only); no outbox record ever approaches 256KiB (payloads by reference); reload/cold-start hydrates complete; migration path tested; the current truncation-marker tests are re-worked to assert the NEW contract (complete storage, bounded index) rather than the old caps. comments.text:
DESIGN (kmpq lane, 2026-09-02/03):

NEW CONTRACT: complete terminal text lives ONCE, in the durable retained
payload (run-payload:* chunked keys, unbounded total). Memory rows + outbox
records hold bounded summaries + retainedPayloadRef ONLY; the thread VIEW
hydrates the complete response from the journal on open.

S1 threads.js (row writer): commitThreadTerminal terminal rows gain an
optional retainedPayloadRef (persisted when the terminal carries one).
Content rule per terminal row: utf8Bytes <= MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES (240KiB, stays a
per-ROW summary bound, byte-complete as today) -> store byte-complete;
larger WITH retainedPayloadRef -> row content = bounded digest (~16KiB,
never-silent) + ref on the row (index/summary + ref only, row stays light);
larger WITHOUT a durable ref (demo/board/direct) -> today's boundText marker
behaviour (nothing else holds it; marker honest).

S2 durable-runs.js settle()/outbox (stall fix): the outbox no longer embeds a
near-bound content copy. threadTerminal.content in the OUTBOX = bounded
digest only; retainedPayloadRef rides threadTerminal. Envelope fields
(toolCalls/skills/citations/serverToolEvents) are bounded at outbox build
(same caps threads.js commit applies). The serialized-size shrink loop +
fail-loud content machinery goes away: records never approach 256KiB because
payloads never live there (any result size fits).

S3 durable-runs.js processOutbox(): before commitThread, when
threadTerminal.retainedPayloadRef is present, resolve the FULL text from the
chunked payload (readJsonPayload) and pass payload.result as content, so the
memory thread row is byte-complete up to its own budget for normal answers
(and S1 digests only genuinely over-budget text). Crash-safe: payload is
written BEFORE the outbox; recovery re-resolves.

S4 thread view hydration (thread-run-view.js + thread.get): terminal
assistant/error body rows whose execution log terminal row carries a fuller
payload.result than the stored content get content replaced with the complete
payload text at view build (listLogs already hydrates terminal payloads for
viewed executions, so this adds no I/O). Missing-terminal reconciliation
prefers terminalRow.payload.result over the record preview. This is the
migration path: existing truncated rows (240KiB marker text) backfill from
the journal where the complete text exists; where it does not, the marker
stays honest.

CONTRACT FLIP (this lane supersedes the truncation contract pinned on main):
outbox tests now assert content-by-reference (small outbox at ANY result
size, full text in payload), thread-row tests assert byte-complete <= the
row summary bound + digest+ref above it, and the view tests assert the
reopened thread renders the COMPLETE 10MiB response from the journal.
Falsification: 10MiB response -> outbox << 256KiB, thread row < 256KiB with
summary+ref, listLogs terminal payload.result length == 10MiB, reopened view
messages carry the full text; migration row (legacy marker text) backfills.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
DESIGN — task-level tab-tools bundle (one card per tab step)

Requirement shape: the bundle reuses the EXISTING permissionRequirement shape the conversation already renders — { reason, permissions, grantOrigins, grantGlobal } — so no new card component, no new requirement type on the conversation side. The bundle ask is: permissions = whichever of [tabs, tabGroups] are still missing; grantOrigins = the denial's own sites union the canonical origins of the owner's currently open web tabs, minus sites already browser-control-granted; grantGlobal passes through only when the denial is genuinely origin-less (a chrome:// tab). A bounded marker field bundle:tab-tools identifies the offer; the card key derives from the content as today.

Where the SW offers it (denial path): every model-run permission pause routes through waitForInlinePermissionDecision (service-worker.js). The offer fires there, gated to denials of the tab family (list_tabs, list_tab_groups, group_tabs, update_tab_group, ungroup_tabs, move_tab_to_group — passed as the selected tool name via the onPermissionRequest hook) whose requirement is permission-shaped (no approvals, no hostOrigins). The offer is MEMOIZED per executionId: the first tab-family denial in a run mints the bundle from live state; any later tab-family denial in the same run reuses the exact minted requirement. The offer stamps the denial's permissionRequirement object IN PLACE — agent.js and the retained tool result share that exact object, so the live approval-request card, the tool-result event, the journaled row, and the reopened thread stay byte-identical (one card everywhere, incl. the denied path).

Allow grants everything in ONE gesture: approvePermissionRequirement is unchanged — one chrome.permissions.request carrying the union permissions (plus any host patterns), then one browser-control.set for the grantOrigins. The bundle simply rides the existing owner-gesture path (trusted-click + user-activation gated), never a new grant route.

Second tab tool, no new card: after Allow, tabs+tabGroups+the sites' browser control are all in place, so the second tool's pre-check finds nothing missing and runs (no denial, no card). A second tab-tool denial BEFORE a decision (a re-run) reuses the memoized requirement -> same card key -> the conversation merges it into the existing card and shares the owner's one click across both paused calls.

Per-tool floor: the builder returns null for non-family tools, non-permission denials, a bundle that would ask nothing, or any failure reading tabs/permissions — the denial is left untouched and the per-tool card renders exactly as today.

Decline: the existing deny path — run.resolve-inline-approval approve:false, terminal '[tool] DENIED by owner', nothing granted. The card's sticky-denied state means a re-denial of the same bundle does not nag again.

Owner-gesture-only (source pin): the bundle exists only as a requirement shape rendered on the owner's card. No new model route, no new tool. A test asserts the model tool-registry files in extension/lib (browser-tools.js, management-tools.js, tool-catalog.js, lazy-tool-protocol.js, chrome-tool-capabilities.js, tool-selection.js, capabilities.js, bundled-tool-packages.js) never name the bundle id or builder.

description:
## [CAP-FB-20260902-DELEGATION-STEP-OFF-BY-ONE-01] The delegation ledger charges a run one iteration fewer than it consumed, so a subtree can exceed its cap while the ledger reads within it
- Feedback: 2026-09-02 — KAT-AGENT-DELEGATION-RED-01 worker, measured on the x4 delegation run: three executed children really consumed 6+6+2 = 14 outer iterations against a cap of 12, while the ledger read `{own:1, descendants:11, total:12, cap:12}`. Cause: `delegationState.step` tracks agent-do's 0-based step index (the `thinking` hook in `extension/background/service-worker.js`), so every accounting read is one low. Pre-existing — the hook predates CAP-FB-20260901-RUN-BUDGET-EVERY-ITEM-01.
- Updated: 2026-09-02 08:10 UTC
- Status: OPEN
- Resume: —
- Priority: P1
- Owner: unassigned
- Workspace: none
- Branch: none
- Base: —
- Candidate: —
- Shipping: —
- Acceptance: The iterations a run has consumed and the iterations its subtree has spent are counted from 1, so `remaining` in `extension/lib/agent-delegation.js` is never larger than the truth; a delegation subtree can never execute more outer iterations than its cap; the audited ledger's `total` equals the outer iterations actually consumed (asserted by driving the x4 delegation KAT and comparing the ledger against the counted `thinking` events). No child's cap grows as a result of the fix (a tighter count means fewer, never more).
  - Context: `extension/background/service-worker.js` updates `activeDelegationRuns.get(executionId).step` from agent-do's `thinking` progress event, whose `step` is 0-based; `extension/lib/agent-delegation.js` computes `remaining = maxIterations - step - childSpend` (`:115`, `:148`) and `assertDelegationSpendWithinCap` (terminal fence) reads the same numbers. The pure module is correct given its inputs — the defect is the input. What must NOT change: the admission-time guard (`MIN_REMAINING_ITERATIONS`) and `CHILD_ITERATION_CAP` semantics; the terminal fence; the KAT's five re-baselined assertions from KAT-AGENT-DELEGATION-RED-01 must still pass.
  - Reproduce today: `deno run -A scripts/kat-agent-delegation.ts` and read its audit lines — `caps 6/6/2 at remaining 12/7/2` shows the parent's remaining falling 12→7 after a child that ran its full cap of 6 (it should fall to 6 or lower).
  - Files: `extension/background/service-worker.js` (the `thinking` hook: record `step + 1`, or record the count of steps observed rather than the index — one place, with a comment naming the 0-based source), `extension/lib/agent-delegation.js` (no change expected; add an assertion that `step` is a count, not an index), `tests/agent-delegation*.test.ts` (a test that a run reporting steps 0..N has consumed N+1), `scripts/kat-agent-delegation.ts` (assert the ledger total equals the counted iterations).
  - Steps: (1) unit RED-first: "a run that reported thinking steps 0,1,2 has consumed 3 iterations" and "a subtree never executes more outer iterations than its cap". (2) fix the hook. (3) re-run the delegation KAT (must stay 61/61) and record the corrected audit line in History.

  - Full suite: `npm run test:all` green at the tip.
  - Constraints: the count may only tighten the budget, never loosen it; the terminal fence stays; no fixed debugging port.
